source.title: Gesamtfragenkatalog zum Test „Leben in Deutschland“ und zum „Einbürgerungstest“

de.q: In Deutschland dürfen Menschen offen etwas gegen die Regierung sagen, weil …

en.q: In Germany, people may openly say things against the government because …
o: people have the right to vote.

explanation.en: Freedom of speech (Meinungsfreiheit) is one of the most important fundamental rights guaranteed by Article 5 of the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz). It means every person in Germany has the right to freely express their opinions in speech, writing, and images — including criticism of the government. This right is essential to a functioning democracy.
explanation.de: In Deutschland gilt Meinungsfreiheit (Art. 5 GG) — Menschen dürfen offen Kritik an der Regierung äußern.

de.q: In Deutschland können Eltern bis zum 14. Lebensjahr ihres Kindes entscheiden, ob es in der Schule am …

en.q: In Germany, until their child turns 14, parents can decide whether the child takes part at school in …

explanation.en: Under German law, parents have the right to decide whether their child participates in religious education at school until the child turns 14. After age 14, the child can decide for themselves whether to attend religious classes (this is called "Religionsmündigkeit" — religious maturity). All other school subjects like history, politics, and languages are mandatory.
explanation.de: Eltern können bis zum 14. Lebensjahr ihres Kindes entscheiden, ob es am Religionsunterricht teilnimmt; danach entscheidet das Kind selbst.

de.q: Deutschland ist ein Rechtsstaat. Was ist damit gemeint?
o: Alle Einwohnerinnen/Einwohner und der Staat müssen sich an die Gesetze halten.
Der Staat muss sich nicht an die Gesetze halten.
Nur Deutsche müssen die Gesetze befolgen.

en.q: Germany is a state governed by the rule of law (Rechtsstaat). What does this mean?
o: All inhabitants and the state must abide by the laws.
The state does not have to abide by the laws.
Only Germans have to obey the laws.

explanation.en: The term "Rechtsstaat" (rule of law / constitutional state) means that the government itself is bound by the law — it cannot act arbitrarily. Everyone, including the state and all its institutions, must follow the law. This principle is a cornerstone of German democracy and is established in the Basic Law.
explanation.de: Ein Rechtsstaat bedeutet, dass sowohl die Bürgerinnen und Bürger als auch der Staat selbst an geltende Gesetze gebunden sind.

de.q: Welches Recht gehört zu den Grundrechten in Deutschland?

en.q: Which right is one of the fundamental rights (Grundrechte) in Germany?

explanation.en: Freedom of expression (Meinungsfreiheit) is a fundamental right protected by Article 5 of the Basic Law. The other options — the right to bear arms, vigilantism (literally "fist law"), and self-help justice — are not fundamental rights in Germany. In fact, vigilantism and self-help justice are illegal. Germany does not have a constitutional right to bear arms like the United States.
explanation.de: Die Meinungsfreiheit ist eines der in Deutschland garantierten Grundrechte.

de.q: Wahlen in Deutschland sind frei. Was bedeutet das?
o: Man darf Geld annehmen, wenn man dafür eine bestimmte Kandidatin/einen bestimmten Kandidaten wählt.
Nur Personen, die noch nie im Gefängnis waren, dürfen wählen.
Die Wählerin/der Wähler darf bei der Wahl weder beeinflusst noch zu einer bestimmten Stimmabgabe gezwungen werden und keine Nachteile durch die Wahl haben.

en.q: Elections in Germany are free. What does that mean?
o: You may accept money if in return you vote for a particular candidate.
Only people who have never been in prison may vote.
Voters may neither be influenced nor forced to vote in a particular way in the election, and must not suffer any disadvantage as a result of voting.
All people entitled to vote must vote.

explanation.en: German elections follow five principles: they are universal, direct, free, equal, and secret (allgemein, unmittelbar, frei, gleich, geheim). "Free" means voters cannot be pressured, bribed, or forced to vote in any particular way. There is no compulsory voting in Germany — voting is a right, not an obligation. Accepting money for votes is illegal.
explanation.de: Freie Wahlen bedeuten, dass niemand beim Wählen beeinflusst, gezwungen oder benachteiligt werden darf.

de.q: Wie heißt die deutsche Verfassung?

en.q: What is the German constitution called?

explanation.en: The German constitution is called the "Grundgesetz" (Basic Law). It was adopted on May 23, 1949 and was originally intended as a temporary constitution for West Germany until reunification. After reunification in 1990, it became the constitution for all of Germany. It was deliberately not called "Verfassung" (constitution) to emphasize its provisional nature, but today it functions fully as Germany's constitution.
explanation.de: Die deutsche Verfassung heißt Grundgesetz.

de.q: Welches Recht gehört zu den Grundrechten, die nach der deutschen Verfassung garantiert werden? Das Recht auf …

en.q: Which right is one of the fundamental rights (Grundrechte) guaranteed by the German constitution? The right to …

explanation.en: Freedom of faith and conscience (Article 4 of the Basic Law) is a fundamental right in Germany. While the right to work and housing are important societal goals, they are not guaranteed as fundamental rights in the Basic Law. The right to entertainment is not a constitutional right at all.
explanation.de: Die Glaubens- und Gewissensfreiheit ist ein durch das Grundgesetz garantiertes Grundrecht.

de.q: Was steht nicht im Grundgesetz von Deutschland?
o: Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar.
Alle sollen gleich viel Geld haben.
Jeder Mensch darf seine Meinung sagen.
Alle sind vor dem Gesetz gleich.

en.q: What is not in the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz)?
o: Everyone should have the same amount of money.
Every person may state their opinion.
All people are equal before the law.

explanation.en: The Basic Law guarantees human dignity (Article 1), freedom of expression (Article 5), and equality before the law (Article 3). However, it does NOT guarantee that everyone should have the same amount of money. Germany has a social market economy which allows for economic differences while providing a social safety net.
explanation.de: Das Grundgesetz garantiert die Würde des Menschen, Meinungsfreiheit und Gleichheit vor dem Gesetz — nicht aber materielle Gleichheit ('gleich viel Geld').

de.q: Welches Grundrecht gilt in Deutschland nur für Ausländerinnen/Ausländer? Das Grundrecht auf …

en.q: Which fundamental right (Grundrecht) applies in Germany only to foreigners? The fundamental right to …

explanation.en: The right to asylum (Article 16a of the Basic Law) is the only fundamental right that applies exclusively to foreigners. It gives politically persecuted people the right to seek protection in Germany. All other listed rights — family protection, human dignity, and freedom of opinion — apply to all people in Germany, regardless of nationality.
explanation.de: Das Asylrecht ist ein Grundrecht, das in Deutschland ausschließlich für Ausländerinnen und Ausländer gilt.

de.q: Was ist mit dem deutschen Grundgesetz vereinbar?

en.q: What is compatible with the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz)?

explanation.en: Among the listed options, only fines (Geldstrafe) are compatible with the Basic Law. Corporal punishment, torture, and the death penalty are all prohibited. Article 102 explicitly states: "The death penalty is abolished." Article 1 (human dignity) and Article 104 prohibit torture and physical punishment by the state.
explanation.de: Eine Geldstrafe ist mit dem Grundgesetz vereinbar — Prügelstrafe, Folter und die Todesstrafe sind verboten.

de.q: Wie wird die Verfassung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland genannt?

en.q: What is the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany called?

explanation.en: This question is similar to Question 6. The German constitution is called the "Grundgesetz" (Basic Law). It was enacted in 1949 and serves as the supreme law of Germany. All other laws must comply with the Basic Law, and the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) ensures this.
explanation.de: Die Verfassung der Bundesrepublik Deutschland wird Grundgesetz genannt.

de.q: Eine Partei im Deutschen Bundestag will die Pressefreiheit abschaffen. Ist das möglich?
o: Ja, wenn mehr als die Hälfte der Abgeordneten im Bundestag dafür sind.
Ja, aber dazu müssen zwei Drittel der Abgeordneten im Bundestag dafür sein.
Nein, denn die Pressefreiheit ist ein Grundrecht. Sie kann nicht abgeschafft werden.
Nein, denn nur der Bundesrat kann die Pressefreiheit abschaffen.

en.q: A party in the German Bundestag wants to abolish freedom of the press. Is that possible?
o: Yes, if more than half of the members of the Bundestag are in favor.
Yes, but for that two thirds of the members of the Bundestag must be in favor.
No, because freedom of the press is a fundamental right (Grundrecht). It cannot be abolished.
No, because only the Bundesrat can abolish freedom of the press.

explanation.en: Press freedom is guaranteed by Article 5 of the Basic Law and is protected by the "eternity clause" (Ewigkeitsklausel, Article 79 Paragraph 3). This clause means that certain core principles of the Basic Law — including fundamental rights like press freedom — can never be abolished or changed, not even with a unanimous vote in parliament.
explanation.de: Die Pressefreiheit ist ein unveräußerliches Grundrecht und kann nicht abgeschafft werden, auch nicht durch eine Mehrheit im Bundestag.

de.q: Im Parlament steht der Begriff "Opposition" für …
o: die Fraktion mit den meisten Abgeordneten.
alle Parteien, die bei der letzten Wahl die 5%-Hürde erreichen konnten.
alle Abgeordneten, die nicht zu der Regierungspartei/den Regierungsparteien gehören.

en.q: In parliament, the term “opposition” refers to …
o: the parliamentary group (Fraktion) with the most members.
all parties that managed to clear the 5% threshold in the last election.
all members of parliament who do not belong to the governing party/parties.

explanation.en: The opposition consists of all parties and their members in parliament who are not part of the government coalition. The opposition plays a crucial role in German democracy: it monitors the government, proposes alternatives, and holds the ruling parties accountable. A strong opposition is considered essential for a healthy democracy.
explanation.de: Im Parlament bezeichnet 'Opposition' alle Abgeordneten, die nicht zur Regierungspartei bzw. den Regierungsparteien gehören.

de.q: Meinungsfreiheit in Deutschland heißt, dass ich …
o: Passanten auf der Straße beschimpfen darf.
meine Meinung im Internet äußern kann.
Nazi-, Hamas- oder Islamischer Staat-Symbole öffentlich tragen darf.
meine Meinung nur dann äußern darf, solange ich der Regierung nicht widerspreche.

en.q: Freedom of expression in Germany means that I …
o: may insult passers-by on the street.
can express my opinion on the internet.
may publicly wear Nazi, Hamas or Islamic State symbols.
may express my opinion only as long as I do not contradict the government.

explanation.en: Freedom of speech means you can express your opinions freely, including on the internet and even against the government. However, this right has limits: you cannot insult individuals (that is a criminal offense called "Beleidigung"), and displaying symbols of banned organizations like the Nazis, Hamas, or ISIS is illegal in Germany. Note that this question was updated to include Hamas and Islamic State references in recent catalog versions.
explanation.de: Meinungsfreiheit erlaubt es, die eigene Meinung frei zu äußern — verboten sind aber z. B. das öffentliche Zeigen verfassungsfeindlicher Symbole.

de.q: Was verbietet das deutsche Grundgesetz?

en.q: What does the German Basic Law (Grundgesetz) prohibit?

explanation.en: The Basic Law explicitly prohibits forced labor (Zwangsarbeit) in Article 12. Military service, free choice of profession, and working abroad are all permitted. In fact, free choice of profession is itself a fundamental right (Article 12). Germany historically experienced forced labor during the Nazi era, which is why this prohibition is explicitly stated.
explanation.de: Das deutsche Grundgesetz verbietet Zwangsarbeit.

de.q: Wann ist die Meinungsfreiheit in Deutschland eingeschränkt?
o: bei der öffentlichen Verbreitung falscher Behauptungen über einzelne Personen

en.q: When is freedom of expression restricted in Germany?
o: when false claims about individual people are spread publicly
when opinions are expressed about the Federal Government

explanation.en: While freedom of speech is a fundamental right, it has limits. Spreading false claims about specific individuals (defamation/slander) can be a criminal offense. However, criticizing the government, discussing religions, or criticizing the state are all protected by freedom of speech. The balance between free speech and personal rights is an important principle in German law.
explanation.de: Die Meinungsfreiheit ist eingeschränkt, wenn falsche Tatsachenbehauptungen über konkrete Personen öffentlich verbreitet werden.

de.q: Die deutschen Gesetze verbieten …
o: Ungleichbehandlung der Bürgerinnen und Bürger durch den Staat.

en.q: German laws prohibit …
o: unequal treatment of citizens by the state.

explanation.en: German law prohibits the state from treating citizens unequally (discrimination). This is established in Article 3 of the Basic Law: "All persons are equal before the law." Freedom of opinion, the right to petition, and freedom of assembly are all protected rights — they are NOT prohibited.
explanation.de: Die deutschen Gesetze verbieten die Ungleichbehandlung von Bürgerinnen und Bürgern durch den Staat.

de.q: Welches Grundrecht ist in Artikel 1 des Grundgesetzes der Bundesrepublik Deutschland garantiert?

en.q: Which fundamental right (Grundrecht) is guaranteed in Article 1 of the Basic Law (Grundgesetz) of the Federal Republic of Germany?

explanation.en: Article 1 of the Basic Law states: "Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar" — "Human dignity shall be inviolable." This is the most important article in the entire constitution and is protected by the eternity clause (it can never be changed or removed). The right to life is in Article 2, freedom of religion in Article 4, and freedom of expression in Article 5.
explanation.de: Artikel 1 des Grundgesetzes garantiert die Unantastbarkeit der Menschenwürde.

de.q: Was versteht man unter dem Recht der "Freizügigkeit" in Deutschland?
o: Man darf sich seinen Wohnort selbst aussuchen.
Man darf sich für eine andere Religion entscheiden.
Man darf sich in der Öffentlichkeit nur leicht bekleidet bewegen.

en.q: What is meant by the right of “freedom of movement” (Freizügigkeit) in Germany?
o: You may choose your place of residence yourself.
You may decide on a different religion.
You may only move about in public lightly dressed.

explanation.en: "Freizügigkeit" (freedom of movement, Article 11 of the Basic Law) means that German citizens have the right to freely choose where to live and work within Germany. This was historically significant because in the GDR (East Germany), citizens were not free to choose their residence or travel freely. The right to change professions is covered by Article 12 (freedom of occupation).
explanation.de: Das Recht der Freizügigkeit bedeutet, dass man seinen Wohnort in Deutschland frei wählen darf.

de.q: Eine Partei in Deutschland verfolgt das Ziel, eine Diktatur zu errichten. Sie ist dann …

en.q: A party in Germany pursues the goal of establishing a dictatorship. It is then …
o: oriented towards the rule of law.

explanation.en: Any party that aims to establish a dictatorship is unconstitutional (verfassungswidrig). The Basic Law protects Germany's democratic order, and Article 21 allows the Federal Constitutional Court to ban parties that seek to undermine or abolish the free democratic basic order. This provision exists because of Germany's experience with the Nazi party, which used democratic processes to destroy democracy itself.
explanation.de: Eine Partei, die eine Diktatur errichten will, verstößt gegen die freiheitlich-demokratische Grundordnung und ist damit verfassungswidrig.

de.q: Welches ist das Wappen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.q: Which is the coat of arms of the Federal Republic of Germany?

explanation.en: The coat of arms of Germany (Bundeswappen) features a black eagle with red beak and claws on a golden (yellow) shield. The eagle has been a symbol of German sovereignty for centuries, dating back to the Holy Roman Empire. The current design was adopted in 1950 for the Federal Republic of Germany.
explanation.de: Das richtige Bild zeigt den einköpfigen Bundesadler auf goldenem Schild, das offizielle Wappen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.

de.q: Was für eine Staatsform hat Deutschland?

en.q: What form of government does Germany have?

explanation.en: Germany is a republic, meaning its head of state (the Federal President) is elected, not a hereditary monarch. Germany became a republic in 1918 when Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated at the end of World War I. The Weimar Republic was followed by the Nazi dictatorship, and after WWII, the Federal Republic of Germany was established in 1949.
explanation.de: Deutschland ist eine Republik.

de.q: In Deutschland sind die meisten Erwerbstätigen …
o: selbstständig mit einer eigenen Firma tätig.
bei einer Firma oder Behörde beschäftigt.

en.q: In Germany, most people in work are …
o: working on a voluntary basis for a federal state.
employed by a company or a public authority.

explanation.en: The vast majority of working people in Germany are employees (Arbeitnehmer) working for companies or government agencies. While small family businesses and self-employment exist, most people are in regular employment relationships with companies, institutions, or public authorities. Volunteering (Ehrenamt) is unpaid and not counted as employment.
explanation.de: Die meisten Erwerbstätigen in Deutschland sind bei einer Firma oder Behörde angestellt, nicht selbstständig.

de.q: Wie viele Bundesländer hat die Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.q: How many federal states does the Federal Republic of Germany have?

explanation.en: Germany consists of 16 federal states (Bundesländer): Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Berlin, Brandenburg, Bremen, Hamburg, Hesse, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Schleswig-Holstein, and Thuringia. Three of these (Berlin, Hamburg, Bremen) are city-states (Stadtstaaten).
explanation.de: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland hat 16 Bundesländer.

de.q: Was ist kein Bundesland der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.q: What is not a federal state of the Federal Republic of Germany?

explanation.en: Alsace-Lorraine (Elsass-Lothringen) is not a German federal state — it is a region in France. It was part of Germany from 1871 to 1918 and again during the Nazi occupation (1940–1945), but has been French territory since the end of WWII. All the other options are legitimate German federal states.
explanation.de: Elsass-Lothringen ist kein deutsches Bundesland, sondern eine historische Region in Frankreich.

de.q: Deutschland ist …

en.q: Germany is …
o: a democratic and social federal state.
a social and socialist federal state.

explanation.en: Article 20 of the Basic Law defines Germany as a "demokratischer und sozialer Bundesstaat" — a democratic and social federal state. This means Germany is democratic (power comes from the people), social (the state provides for those in need), and federal (power is shared between the central government and the 16 states). Germany is neither communist, monarchist, nor socialist.
explanation.de: Deutschland ist laut Grundgesetz ein demokratischer und sozialer Bundesstaat.

de.q: Deutschland ist …

en.q: Germany is …

explanation.en: Germany is a federal state (Bundesstaat), meaning it is composed of several partially sovereign states (Bundesländer) that share power with the central government. The GDR (East Germany) was a socialist state, but unified Germany is not. Germany has not been a monarchy since 1918 and has not been a dictatorship since 1945.
explanation.de: Deutschland ist ein Bundesstaat, bestehend aus 16 Bundesländern.

de.q: Wer wählt in Deutschland die Abgeordneten zum Bundestag?

en.q: Who elects the members of the Bundestag in Germany?

explanation.en: Members of the Bundestag (German parliament) are elected directly by the eligible voters (wahlberechtigtes Volk). Every German citizen aged 18 or older has the right to vote in federal elections. Elections are held every four years. The military, business sector, and government administration have no special role in electing parliament members.
explanation.de: Der Bundestag wird direkt vom wahlberechtigten Volk gewählt.

de.q: Welches Tier ist das Wappentier der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.q: Which animal is the heraldic animal of the Federal Republic of Germany?

explanation.en: The eagle (Adler) is the heraldic animal of Germany, known as the "Bundesadler" (Federal Eagle). It has been a symbol of German authority since the Holy Roman Empire. The Berlin bear is the symbol of the city of Berlin, the lion appears on the coat of arms of several German states (like Bavaria and Hesse), and the horse is the symbol of Lower Saxony.
explanation.de: Der Adler ist das Wappentier der Bundesrepublik Deutschland.

de.q: Was ist kein Merkmal unserer Demokratie?

en.q: What is not a feature of our democracy?

explanation.en: Press censorship (Pressezensur) is NOT a feature of democracy — it is the opposite. In a democracy, the press must be free to report without government censorship. Regular elections, freedom of opinion, and multiple parties are all essential features of a functioning democracy. Press freedom is specifically protected by Article 5 of the Basic Law.
explanation.de: Pressezensur ist kein Merkmal unserer Demokratie — im Gegenteil, Deutschland garantiert Pressefreiheit.

de.q: Die Zusammenarbeit von Parteien zur Bildung einer Regierung nennt man in Deutschland …

en.q: In Germany, cooperation between parties to form a government is called …

explanation.en: When two or more parties work together to form a government, this alliance is called a "Koalition" (coalition). Since no single party usually wins an absolute majority in German elections, coalitions are very common. The parties negotiate a coalition agreement (Koalitionsvertrag) that outlines their shared political goals. A "Fraktion" is a parliamentary group of one party, and a "Ministerium" is a government ministry.

de.q: Was ist keine staatliche Gewalt in Deutschland?

en.q: What is not a branch of state power in Germany?

explanation.en: Germany has three branches of government (Gewaltenteilung): Legislative (Gesetzgebung — makes laws, e.g., Bundestag), Executive (Regierung — enforces laws, e.g., government/police), and Judiciary (Rechtsprechung — interprets laws, e.g., courts). The press is NOT a branch of state power. However, the media is sometimes informally called the "fourth estate" (vierte Gewalt) because of its important watchdog role.

de.q: Welche Aussage ist richtig? In Deutschland …
o: sind Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften voneinander getrennt.
ist der Staat abhängig von den Religionsgemeinschaften.
bilden Staat und Religionsgemeinschaften eine Einheit.

en.q: Which statement is correct? In Germany …
o: the state and religious communities are separate from each other.
the state is dependent on religious communities.
the state and religious communities form a single entity.

explanation.en: Germany practices separation of church and state. While Germany is not as strictly secular as France (churches can collect taxes through the state, and religious education is offered in public schools), the state and religious communities are constitutionally separate. No religion has governmental authority, and the state does not favor any particular religion.

de.q: Was ist Deutschland nicht?

en.q: What is Germany not?
o: a state governed by the rule of law (Rechtsstaat)

explanation.en: Germany is NOT a monarchy. It is a democracy, a constitutional state (Rechtsstaat), and a welfare state (Sozialstaat). Germany ended its monarchy in 1918 when Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated at the end of World War I. Since then, Germany has been a republic with an elected head of state (the Federal President).

de.q: Womit finanziert der deutsche Staat die Sozialversicherung?

en.q: What does the German state use to finance social insurance?

explanation.en: Social insurance in Germany is financed through social security contributions (Sozialabgaben), which are automatically deducted from employees' gross salaries. Both employers and employees contribute approximately equal shares. These contributions fund health insurance, pension insurance, unemployment insurance, long-term care insurance, and accident insurance. Church tax is a separate voluntary payment, and donations/membership fees play no role in public social insurance.

de.q: Welche Maßnahme schafft in Deutschland soziale Sicherheit?

en.q: Which measure provides social security in Germany?

explanation.en: Health insurance (Krankenversicherung) is part of the German social security system (Sozialversicherung). It is mandatory for all residents of Germany. Car insurance, property insurance, and liability insurance are private insurances that protect against specific risks but are not part of the social security system. Germany's social insurance has five pillars: health, pension, unemployment, long-term care, and accident insurance.

de.q: Wie werden die Regierungschefinnen/Regierungschefs der meisten Bundesländer in Deutschland genannt?

en.q: What are the heads of government of most federal states in Germany called?

explanation.en: The heads of government in most German federal states are called "Ministerpräsident/in" (Minister-President). The exceptions are the three city-states: Berlin's head of government is the "Regierende/r Bürgermeister/in" (Governing Mayor), Hamburg's is the "Erste/r Bürgermeister/in" (First Mayor), and Bremen's is the "Präsident/in des Senats und Bürgermeister/in" (President of the Senate and Mayor).

de.q: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist ein demokratischer und sozialer …

en.q: The Federal Republic of Germany is a democratic and social …

explanation.en: As stated in Article 20 of the Basic Law, Germany is a "demokratischer und sozialer Bundesstaat" (democratic and social federal state). A Bundesstaat (federal state) is different from a Staatenbund (confederation — a loose alliance of independent states like the EU) and a Zentralstaat (centralized/unitary state like France). In a federal state, power is shared between a central government and regional governments.

de.q: Was hat jedes deutsche Bundesland?

en.q: What does every German federal state have?

explanation.en: Each German federal state has its own state government (Landesregierung), led by a Minister-President, with its own state parliament (Landtag) and state constitution. However, states do NOT have their own foreign ministers (foreign policy is a federal matter), their own currency (Germany uses the Euro throughout), or their own military (the Bundeswehr is the sole military force for all of Germany).

de.q: Mit welchen Worten beginnt die deutsche Nationalhymne?

en.q: With which words does the German national anthem begin?
o: Joy, beautiful spark of the gods …

explanation.en: The German national anthem uses only the third verse of the "Deutschlandlied" (Song of Germany), written by August Heinrich Hoffmann von Fallersleben in 1841. It begins with "Einigkeit und Recht und Freiheit" (Unity and justice and freedom). "Freude schöner Götterfunken" is from Beethoven's "Ode to Joy" (the EU anthem). "Völker, hört die Signale" is from "The Internationale" (a socialist anthem). "Deutschland einig Vaterland" was from the GDR national anthem.

de.q: Warum gibt es in einer Demokratie mehr als eine Partei?
o: weil dadurch die unterschiedlichen Meinungen der Bürgerinnen und Bürger vertreten werden
damit Bestechung in der Politik begrenzt wird

en.q: Why is there more than one party in a democracy?
o: because this means the different opinions of citizens are represented
so that bribery in politics is limited

explanation.en: Multiple parties exist in a democracy to represent the diversity of opinions and interests among citizens. Different groups of people have different values, priorities, and political views, and parties serve as vehicles for channeling these views into the political process. A one-party system would not represent this diversity and is characteristic of authoritarian regimes.

de.q: Wer beschließt in Deutschland ein neues Gesetz?

en.q: Who passes a new law in Germany?

explanation.en: New laws in Germany are enacted by parliament (the Bundestag, often with participation of the Bundesrat). While the government can propose laws, only parliament has the authority to pass them through a vote. Courts interpret and apply laws but do not create them. The police enforce laws but have no legislative power. This separation of powers is a fundamental principle of the Rechtsstaat.

de.q: Wann kann in Deutschland eine Partei verboten werden?
o: wenn ihr Wahlkampf zu teuer ist
wenn sie gegen die Verfassung kämpft
wenn sie Kritik am Staatsoberhaupt äußert
wenn ihr Programm eine neue Richtung vorschlägt

en.q: When can a party be banned in Germany?
o: if its election campaign is too expensive
if it fights against the constitution
if it criticises the head of state
if its program proposes a new direction

explanation.en: A party can only be banned in Germany if it actively seeks to undermine or abolish the free democratic basic order (freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung). Only the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) can ban a party — no other body has this authority. Criticizing politicians, proposing new policies, or spending money on campaigns are all legitimate political activities. A notable recent example was the banning attempt against the NPD.

de.q: Wen kann man als Bürgerin/Bürger in Deutschland nicht direkt wählen?

en.q: As a citizen in Germany, whom can you not elect directly?

explanation.en: German citizens cannot directly elect the Federal President (Bundespräsident/in). The President is elected by the Federal Convention (Bundesversammlung), a special body consisting of all Bundestag members plus an equal number of delegates chosen by the state parliaments. Citizens directly elect members of the Bundestag, state parliaments (Landtage), and the European Parliament.

de.q: Zu welcher Versicherung gehört die Pflegeversicherung?

en.q: Which type of insurance does long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) belong to?

explanation.en: Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) is one of the five pillars of the German social insurance system (Sozialversicherung). The five pillars are: health insurance (Krankenversicherung), pension insurance (Rentenversicherung), unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung), long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung), and accident insurance (Unfallversicherung). Home contents insurance and liability insurance are private, voluntary insurances.

de.q: Der deutsche Staat hat viele Aufgaben. Welche Aufgabe gehört dazu?
o: Er versorgt alle Einwohnerinnen und Einwohner kostenlos mit Zeitungen.

en.q: The German state has many tasks. Which task is one of them?
o: It provides all inhabitants with newspapers free of charge.

explanation.en: Building infrastructure like roads and public institutions like schools is a core task of the German state. The state does NOT sell food and clothing (that is done by private businesses), does NOT provide free newspapers (the press is independent), and does NOT produce cars and buses (that is done by private manufacturers like Volkswagen, BMW, etc.). Germany has a social market economy where the private sector handles most commercial activity.

de.q: Der deutsche Staat hat viele Aufgaben. Welche Aufgabe gehört nicht dazu?
o: Er bezahlt für alle Staatsangehörigen Urlaubsreisen.

en.q: The German state has many tasks. Which task is not one of them?
o: It pays for holiday trips for all its citizens.

explanation.en: The German state does NOT pay for vacation trips for all citizens. However, the state does pay child benefit (Kindergeld — a monthly payment for each child), supports museums and cultural institutions, and funds sports and athletes. In the GDR, the state subsidized vacation trips for workers, but this is not the case in modern Germany's social market economy.

de.q: Welches Organ gehört nicht zu den Verfassungsorganen Deutschlands?

en.q: Which body is not one of Germany's constitutional bodies (Verfassungsorgane)?

explanation.en: Germany's constitutional organs (Verfassungsorgane) are: the Bundestag (parliament), the Bundesrat (Federal Council representing the states), the Federal President (Bundespräsident/in), the Federal Government (Bundesregierung), and the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht). A "Bürgerversammlung" (citizens' assembly) is NOT a constitutional organ — it is a concept from local or participatory democracy but not part of Germany's constitutional structure.

de.q: Wer bestimmt in Deutschland die Schulpolitik?

en.q: Who determines school policy in Germany?

explanation.en: Educational policy in Germany is determined by the federal states (Bundesländer), not the central government. This is called "Kulturhoheit der Länder" (cultural sovereignty of the states). Each state has its own Ministry of Education and sets its own curriculum, school system, and educational standards. This is why school systems can differ significantly between states — for example, the number of years in primary school or the types of secondary schools available.

de.q: Die Wirtschaftsform in Deutschland nennt man …

en.q: The economic system in Germany is called …

explanation.en: Germany's economic system is the "soziale Marktwirtschaft" (social market economy). This model was developed by Ludwig Erhard after WWII and combines free market principles with social welfare policies. Businesses operate freely and compete in the market, but the state intervenes to provide social security, prevent monopolies, and ensure fair working conditions. The GDR (East Germany) had a "Planwirtschaft" (planned economy), where the state controlled all economic activity.

de.q: Zu einem demokratischen Rechtsstaat gehört es nicht, dass …
o: Menschen sich kritisch über die Regierung äußern können.
Menschen von einer Privatpolizei ohne Grund verhaftet werden.
jemand ein Verbrechen begeht und deshalb verhaftet wird.

en.q: It is not part of a democratic state governed by the rule of law (Rechtsstaat) that …
o: people can express criticism of the government.
citizens are allowed to go on peaceful demonstrations.
people are arrested by a private police force without reason.
someone commits a crime and is arrested for it.

explanation.en: In a democratic Rechtsstaat, only the state police can arrest people, and only with legal justification. A "private police" arresting people without reason would be illegal and undemocratic. Criticizing the government, peaceful demonstrations, and lawful arrests for crimes are all normal parts of a democratic society.

de.q: Was bedeutet "Volkssouveränität"? Alle Staatsgewalt geht vom …

en.q: What does “popular sovereignty” (Volkssouveränität) mean? All state authority is derived from the …

explanation.en: "Volkssouveränität" (popular sovereignty) is established in Article 20 of the Basic Law: "Alle Staatsgewalt geht vom Volke aus" — "All state authority emanates from the people." This means the people are the ultimate source of political power. They exercise this power through elections and votes. The Bundestag represents the people, but the power originates from the citizens themselves.

de.q: Was bedeutet "Rechtsstaat" in Deutschland?
o: Die Bürgerinnen und Bürger entscheiden über Gesetze.
Der Staat muss die Gesetze einhalten.

en.q: What does “state governed by the rule of law” (Rechtsstaat) mean in Germany?
o: The state must abide by the laws.

explanation.en: "Rechtsstaat" literally translates to "law state" or "state of law." It means the state and all its institutions are bound by law — the government cannot act arbitrarily but must follow legal rules. This is different from "the state is right" (a common misunderstanding) or "only right-wing parties" (a play on the word "Recht" which can mean both "law/right" and "right-wing").

de.q: Was ist keine staatliche Gewalt in Deutschland?

en.q: What is not a branch of state power in Germany?

explanation.en: Germany's state power is divided into three branches: Legislative (law-making), Executive (Exekutive, law-enforcing), and Judiciary (Judikative, law-interpreting). "Direktive" is not a real branch of government — it is the trick answer.

de.q: Was zeigt dieses Bild?

en.q: What does this picture show?
o: the seat of the Bundestag in Berlin
the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) in Karlsruhe

questions.credit: Christian David / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

explanation.en: The picture shows the Reichstag building in Berlin, which houses the German Bundestag (federal parliament) — recognizable by its glass dome.

de.q: Welches Amt gehört in Deutschland zur Gemeindeverwaltung?

en.q: Which office in Germany is part of the municipal administration (Gemeindeverwaltung)?

explanation.en: The Ordnungsamt (public order office) is a municipal authority responsible for local public order and safety. The Pfarramt is religious, the Finanzamt is a state tax office, and the Auswärtiges Amt is the federal foreign ministry — none are municipal.

de.q: Wer wird meistens zur Präsidentin/zum Präsidenten des Deutschen Bundestages gewählt?
o: die Ministerpräsidentin/der Ministerpräsident des größten Bundeslandes
eine Abgeordnete/ein Abgeordneter der stärksten Fraktion

en.q: Who is usually elected President of the German Bundestag?
o: the Minister-President (Ministerpräsident) of the largest federal state
a member of the largest parliamentary group (Fraktion)

explanation.en: By convention, the President of the Bundestag is a member of the strongest parliamentary group (Fraktion), not necessarily the oldest MP or a former Chancellor.

de.q: Wer ernennt in Deutschland die Ministerinnen/die Minister der Bundesregierung?

en.q: Who appoints the ministers of the Federal Government in Germany?
o: the President of the Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht)

explanation.en: The Federal President formally appoints and dismisses federal ministers, on the proposal of the Chancellor.

de.q: Vor wie vielen Jahren gab es erstmals eine jüdische Gemeinde auf dem Gebiet des heutigen Deutschlands?

en.q: How many years ago was there a Jewish community on the territory of present-day Germany for the first time?

explanation.en: Jewish communities have existed on German territory for about 1,700 years, with documented evidence dating to Roman-era Cologne in 321 CE — among the oldest Jewish settlements in Europe north of the Alps.

de.q: In Deutschland gehören der Bundestag und der Bundesrat zur …

en.q: In Germany, the Bundestag and the Bundesrat belong to the …

explanation.en: The Bundestag and Bundesrat are both legislative bodies (Legislative) — they make laws, unlike the executive (government) or judiciary (courts).

de.q: Was bedeutet "Volkssouveränität"?
o: Die Königin/der König herrscht über das Volk.
Das Bundesverfassungsgericht steht über der Verfassung.
Die Interessenverbände üben die Souveränität zusammen mit der Regierung aus.
Die Staatsgewalt geht vom Volke aus.

en.q: What does “popular sovereignty” (Volkssouveränität) mean?
o: The monarch rules over the people.
The Federal Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) stands above the constitution.
Interest groups exercise sovereignty together with the government.
State authority is derived from the people.

explanation.en: Popular sovereignty, enshrined in Article 20 of the Basic Law, means all state authority is derived from the people, exercised through elections and referenda.

de.q: Wenn das Parlament eines deutschen Bundeslandes gewählt wird, nennt man das …

en.q: When the parliament of a German federal state is elected, this is called …

explanation.en: Electing a state parliament (Landtag) is called a Landtagswahl, distinct from municipal, European, or federal elections.

de.q: Was gehört in Deutschland nicht zur Exekutive?

en.q: What is not part of the executive (Exekutive) in Germany?

explanation.en: Courts belong to the judiciary (Judikative), not the executive. Police, tax offices, and ministries are all part of the executive branch.

de.q: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist heute gegliedert in …

en.q: Today, the Federal Republic of Germany is divided into …
o: an eastern state and a western state.
the Federation (Bund), the federal states (Länder) and the municipalities (Kommunen).

explanation.en: Germany's administrative structure has three levels: the federal government (Bund), the 16 states (Länder), and local municipalities (Kommunen).

de.q: Es gehört nicht zu den Aufgaben des Deutschen Bundestages, …

en.q: It is not one of the tasks of the German Bundestag to …

explanation.en: Forming the cabinet is the Chancellor's job, not the Bundestag's. The Bundestag drafts laws, elects the Chancellor, and controls the government.

de.q: Welche Städte haben die größten jüdischen Gemeinden in Deutschland?

en.q: Which cities have the largest Jewish communities in Germany?

explanation.en: Berlin and Munich have Germany's largest Jewish communities today, reflecting post-reunification and post-Soviet immigration patterns.

de.q: Was ist in Deutschland vor allem eine Aufgabe der Bundesländer?

en.q: In Germany, what is primarily a task of the federal states?

explanation.en: Education policy (Schulpolitik) is primarily a state responsibility in Germany, unlike defense, foreign affairs, and much of economic policy, which are federal matters.

de.q: Warum kontrolliert der Staat in Deutschland das Schulwesen?
o: weil es in Deutschland nur staatliche Schulen gibt
weil alle Schülerinnen und Schüler einen Schulabschluss haben müssen
weil es in den Bundesländern verschiedene Schulen gibt
weil es nach dem Grundgesetz seine Aufgabe ist

en.q: Why does the state supervise the school system in Germany?
o: because there are only state schools in Germany
because all pupils must have a school-leaving qualification
because there are different schools in the federal states
because this is its task under the Basic Law (Grundgesetz)

explanation.en: State oversight of schools (Schulaufsicht) is a constitutional duty under the Basic Law, ensuring educational quality and standards nationwide.

de.q: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland hat einen dreistufigen Verwaltungsaufbau. Wie heißt die unterste politische Stufe?

en.q: The Federal Republic of Germany has a three-tier administrative structure. What is the lowest political tier called?

explanation.en: The Gemeinden (municipalities) form the lowest administrative and political level in Germany's three-tier structure of Bund, Länder, and Gemeinden.

de.q: Der deutsche Bundespräsident Gustav Heinemann gibt Helmut Schmidt 1974 die Ernennungsurkunde zum deutschen Bundeskanzler. Was gehört zu den Aufgaben der deutschen Bundespräsidentin/des deutschen Bundespräsidenten?
o: Sie/Er schlägt die Kanzlerin/den Kanzler zur Wahl vor.

en.q: German Federal President (Bundespräsident) Gustav Heinemann hands Helmut Schmidt his certificate of appointment as German Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) in 1974. Which of these is one of the duties of the German Federal President?
o: He or she conducts the business of government.
He or she controls the governing party.
He or she selects the ministers.
He or she proposes the Chancellor (Kanzler) for election.

explanation.en: The Federal President proposes a candidate for Chancellor to the Bundestag for election, and formally appoints the Chancellor and ministers — but does not run the government or select ministers personally.

de.q: Wo hält sich die deutsche Bundeskanzlerin/der deutsche Bundeskanzler am häufigsten auf? Am häufigsten ist sie/er …
o: in Bonn, weil sich dort das Bundeskanzleramt und der Bundestag befinden.
auf Schloss Meseberg, dem Gästehaus der Bundesregierung, um Staatsgäste zu empfangen.
auf Schloss Bellevue, dem Amtssitz der Bundespräsidentin/des Bundespräsidenten, um Staatsgäste zu empfangen.
in Berlin, weil sich dort das Bundeskanzleramt und der Bundestag befinden.

en.q: Where is the German Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) most often found? He or she is most often …
o: in Bonn, because the Federal Chancellery (Bundeskanzleramt) and the Bundestag are located there.
at Meseberg Palace (Schloss Meseberg), the Federal Government's guest house, to receive state guests.
at Bellevue Palace (Schloss Bellevue), the official residence of the Federal President (Bundespräsident), to receive state guests.
in Berlin, because the Federal Chancellery (Bundeskanzleramt) and the Bundestag are located there.

explanation.en: Since the government moved from Bonn to Berlin in 1999, the Chancellor is most often in Berlin, home to both the Chancellery and the Bundestag.

de.q: Wie heißt die jetzige Bundeskanzlerin/der jetzige Bundeskanzler von Deutschland?

en.q: What is the name of the current Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) of Germany?

explanation.en: Friedrich Merz (CDU) has been Federal Chancellor since 2025. Note: this is a current-affairs question the real test updates periodically — always verify the current officeholder before the exam.

de.q: Die beiden größten Fraktionen im Deutschen Bundestag heißen zurzeit …

en.q: The two largest parliamentary groups (Fraktionen) in the German Bundestag are currently …

explanation.en: Following the 2025 federal election, CDU/CSU and AfD are the two largest parliamentary groups. Note: this is a current-affairs question — verify before the exam, as party standings change with each election.

de.q: Wie heißt das Parlament für ganz Deutschland?

en.q: What is the parliament for the whole of Germany called?

explanation.en: The Bundestag is Germany's national parliament. The Bundesversammlung only convenes to elect the President, the Volkskammer was the former East German parliament, and the Bundesgerichtshof is a court.

de.q: Wie heißt Deutschlands heutiges Staatsoberhaupt?

en.q: What is the name of Germany's current head of state?

explanation.en: Frank-Walter Steinmeier is Germany's Federal President (head of state). Note: this is a current-affairs question — verify the current officeholder before the exam.

de.q: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung CDU in Deutschland?

en.q: What does the abbreviation CDU stand for in Germany?

explanation.en: CDU stands for Christlich Demokratische Union (Christian Democratic Union), one of Germany's major political parties.

de.q: Was ist die Bundeswehr?

en.q: What is the Bundeswehr?

explanation.en: The Bundeswehr is Germany's armed forces (the military), not the police, a port, or a citizens' group.

de.q: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung SPD?

en.q: What does the abbreviation SPD stand for?

explanation.en: SPD stands for Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands (Social Democratic Party of Germany), one of Germany's oldest and largest parties.

de.q: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung FDP in Deutschland?

en.q: What does the abbreviation FDP stand for in Germany?

explanation.en: FDP stands for Freie Demokratische Partei (Free Democratic Party), a liberal party in Germany.

de.q: Welches Gericht in Deutschland ist zuständig für die Auslegung des Grundgesetzes?

en.q: Which court in Germany is responsible for interpreting the Basic Law (Grundgesetz)?

explanation.en: The Bundesverfassungsgericht (Federal Constitutional Court), located in Karlsruhe, is responsible for interpreting the Basic Law and reviewing the constitutionality of laws.

de.q: Wer wählt die Bundeskanzlerin/den Bundeskanzler in Deutschland?

en.q: Who elects the Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) in Germany?

explanation.en: The Bundestag elects the Federal Chancellor, on the proposal of the Federal President — not the people directly, the Bundesrat, or the Bundesversammlung (which only elects the President).

de.q: Wer leitet das deutsche Bundeskabinett?

en.q: Who heads the German Federal Cabinet (Bundeskabinett)?

explanation.en: The Federal Chancellor leads the federal cabinet and determines the general policy guidelines (Richtlinienkompetenz).

de.q: Wer wählt die deutsche Bundeskanzlerin/den deutschen Bundeskanzler?

en.q: Who elects the German Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler)?

explanation.en: The Bundestag elects the Federal Chancellor — Germans do not vote for the Chancellor directly.

de.q: Welche Hauptaufgabe hat die deutsche Bundespräsidentin/der deutsche Bundespräsident? Sie/Er …

en.q: What is the main task of the German Federal President (Bundespräsident)? He or she …

explanation.en: The Federal President's main role is representative (a largely ceremonial head of state) — the Chancellor governs, and the Bundestag drafts laws.

de.q: Wer bildet den deutschen Bundesrat?
o: die Ministerinnen und Minister der Bundesregierung

en.q: Who makes up the German Bundesrat?
o: the ministers of the Federal Government
the government representatives of the federal states

explanation.en: The Bundesrat consists of representatives of the state governments (Länder), representing regional interests in federal legislation.

de.q: Wer wählt in Deutschland die Bundespräsidentin/den Bundespräsidenten?

en.q: Who elects the Federal President (Bundespräsident) in Germany?

explanation.en: The Bundesversammlung (Federal Convention) — a special body of Bundestag members and state delegates — elects the Federal President every five years.

de.q: Wer ist das Staatsoberhaupt der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.q: Who is the head of state of the Federal Republic of Germany?

explanation.en: The Federal President is Germany's head of state, a largely ceremonial role, distinct from the Chancellor who heads the government.

de.q: Die parlamentarische Opposition im Deutschen Bundestag …
o: schlägt die Regierungschefinnen/Regierungschefs der Länder vor.

en.q: The parliamentary opposition in the German Bundestag …
o: decides who becomes a federal minister.
determines who sits in the Bundesrat.
proposes the heads of government of the federal states.

explanation.en: The parliamentary opposition's key role is to control and scrutinize the government — it does not appoint ministers or determine Bundesrat/state leadership.

de.q: Wie nennt man in Deutschland die Vereinigung von Abgeordneten einer Partei im Parlament?

en.q: In Germany, what is the association of members of parliament from one party called?

explanation.en: A Fraktion is the parliamentary group formed by members of the same party (or allied parties) in the Bundestag.

de.q: Die deutschen Bundesländer wirken an der Gesetzgebung des Bundes mit durch …

en.q: The German federal states participate in federal legislation through …

explanation.en: The Bundesrat is the chamber through which the states participate in federal lawmaking, giving them a voice in national legislation.

de.q: In Deutschland kann ein Regierungswechsel in einem Bundesland Auswirkungen auf die Bundespolitik haben. Das Regieren wird …
o: schwieriger, wenn sich dadurch die Mehrheit im Bundestag ändert.
leichter, wenn dadurch neue Parteien in den Bundesrat kommen.
schwieriger, wenn dadurch die Mehrheit im Bundesrat verändert wird.
leichter, wenn es sich um ein reiches Bundesland handelt.

en.q: In Germany, a change of government in a federal state can have an impact on federal politics. Governing becomes …
o: more difficult if this changes the majority in the Bundestag.
easier if this brings new parties into the Bundesrat.
more difficult if this changes the majority in the Bundesrat.
easier if it is a wealthy federal state.

explanation.en: Since state governments sit in the Bundesrat, a shift in a state election can change the Bundesrat majority, making federal governing harder if the opposition gains ground there.

de.q: Was bedeutet die Abkürzung CSU in Deutschland?

en.q: What does the abbreviation CSU stand for in Germany?

explanation.en: CSU stands for Christlich Soziale Union (Christian Social Union), the Bavaria-only sister party of the CDU.

de.q: Je mehr "Zweitstimmen" eine Partei bei einer Bundestagswahl bekommt, desto …
o: mehr Direktkandidaten der Partei ziehen ins Parlament ein.
größer ist das Risiko, eine Koalition bilden zu müssen.
mehr Sitze erhält die Partei im Parlament.

en.q: The more “second votes” (Zweitstimmen) a party receives in a federal election (Bundestagswahl), the …
o: fewer first votes (Erststimmen) it can have.
more of the party's direct candidates (Direktkandidaten) enter parliament.
greater the risk of having to form a coalition.
more seats the party receives in parliament.

explanation.en: The Zweitstimme (second vote) determines each party's overall share of Bundestag seats — the more second votes, the more total seats.

de.q: Ab welchem Alter darf man in Deutschland an der Wahl zum Deutschen Bundestag teilnehmen?

en.q: From what age are you allowed to take part in elections to the German Bundestag?

explanation.en: The minimum voting age for federal (Bundestag) elections in Germany is 18.

de.q: Was gilt für die meisten Kinder in Deutschland?

en.q: What applies to most children in Germany?

explanation.en: Compulsory schooling (Schulpflicht) applies to nearly all children in Germany — voting, confidentiality, and religion are not compulsory for children.

de.q: Wie kann jemand, der den Holocaust leugnet, bestraft werden?
o: mit Freiheitsstrafe bis zu fünf Jahren oder mit Geldstrafe

en.q: How can someone who denies the Holocaust be punished?
o: up to 100 hours of community service
not at all, Holocaust denial is allowed
with imprisonment of up to five years or a fine

explanation.en: Holocaust denial is a criminal offense in Germany under §130(3) StGB (Volksverhetzung — incitement to hatred). Anyone who publicly denies, downplays, or approves of the Nazi genocide can face up to 5 years in prison or a fine. This law reflects Germany's historical responsibility for the murder of 6 million Jews. Germany takes this very seriously — it is NOT a matter of free speech but a criminal act.

de.q: Was bezahlt man in Deutschland automatisch, wenn man fest angestellt ist?

en.q: What do you pay automatically in Germany if you are permanently employed?

explanation.en: Permanently employed workers automatically pay into social insurance (Sozialversicherung) — covering health, pension, unemployment, and long-term care.

de.q: Wenn Abgeordnete im Deutschen Bundestag ihre Fraktion wechseln, …
o: dürfen sie nicht mehr an den Sitzungen des Parlaments teilnehmen.
kann die Regierung ihre Mehrheit verlieren.
muss die Bundespräsidentin/der Bundespräsident zuvor ihr/sein Einverständnis geben.
dürfen die Wählerinnen/Wähler dieser Abgeordneten noch einmal wählen.

en.q: If members of the German Bundestag switch their parliamentary group (Fraktion), …
o: they may no longer take part in the sessions of parliament.
the government can lose its majority.
the Federal President (Bundespräsident) must give his or her consent beforehand.
the voters of these members may vote again.

explanation.en: If enough MPs switch groups, the governing coalition can lose its parliamentary majority, since coalitions rely on a specific seat count.

de.q: Wer bezahlt in Deutschland die Sozialversicherungen?

en.q: Who pays for social insurance in Germany?

explanation.en: Social insurance contributions are shared between employers and employees, each paying roughly half.

de.q: Was gehört nicht zur gesetzlichen Sozialversicherung?

en.q: What is not part of statutory social insurance?

explanation.en: Life insurance is a private/optional product, not part of Germany's statutory social insurance system (pension, unemployment, health, and long-term care insurance).

de.q: Gewerkschaften sind Interessenverbände der …

en.q: Trade unions (Gewerkschaften) are associations representing the interests of …

explanation.en: Trade unions (Gewerkschaften) represent the interests of employees (workers), negotiating wages and working conditions with employers.

de.q: Womit kann man in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland geehrt werden, wenn man auf politischem, wirtschaftlichem, kulturellem, geistigem oder sozialem Gebiet eine besondere Leistung erbracht hat? Mit dem …

en.q: What can a person in the Federal Republic of Germany be honored with if they have achieved something outstanding in the political, economic, cultural, intellectual or social field? With the …
o: honorary title “Hero of the German Democratic Republic”

explanation.en: The Bundesverdienstkreuz (Federal Cross of Merit) is Germany's highest honor for outstanding contributions; the other options are either symbols, not awards, or from the former GDR.

de.q: Was wird in Deutschland als "Ampelkoalition" bezeichnet? Die Zusammenarbeit …
o: der Bundestagsfraktionen von CDU und CSU
von SPD, FDP und Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in einer Regierung
von CSU, Die LINKE und Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in einer Regierung
der Bundestagsfraktionen von CDU und SPD

en.q: What is called a “traffic light coalition” (Ampelkoalition) in Germany? The cooperation …
o: of the CDU and CSU parliamentary groups in the Bundestag
of the SPD, FDP and Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in a government
of the CSU, Die LINKE and Bündnis 90/Die Grünen in a government
of the CDU and SPD parliamentary groups in the Bundestag

explanation.en: The "traffic light coalition" (Ampelkoalition) refers to a government of SPD (red), FDP (yellow), and Bündnis 90/Die Grünen (green) — matching traffic light colors.

de.q: Eine Frau in Deutschland verliert ihre Arbeit. Was darf nicht der Grund für diese Entlassung sein?
o: Die Frau ist lange krank und arbeitsunfähig.
Die Frau kam oft zu spät zur Arbeit.
Die Frau erledigt private Sachen während der Arbeitszeit.
Die Frau bekommt ein Kind und ihr Chef weiß das.

en.q: A woman in Germany loses her job. What must not be the reason for this dismissal?
o: The woman has been ill for a long time and is unable to work.
The woman often came to work late.
The woman takes care of private matters during working hours.
The woman is having a baby and her boss knows this.

explanation.en: Pregnancy is legally protected in Germany (Mutterschutz) — dismissing a woman because she is having a child is illegal, unlike the other listed conduct-related reasons.

de.q: Was ist eine Aufgabe von Wahlhelferinnen/Wahlhelfern in Deutschland?
o: Sie helfen alten Menschen bei der Stimmabgabe in der Wahlkabine.
Sie schreiben die Wahlbenachrichtigungen vor der Wahl.
Sie geben Zwischenergebnisse an die Medien weiter.
Sie zählen die Stimmen nach dem Ende der Wahl.

en.q: What is one of the tasks of election workers in Germany?
o: They help elderly people cast their vote in the voting booth.
They write the voter notification cards before the election.
They pass on interim results to the media.
They count the votes after the election has ended.

explanation.en: Election helpers (Wahlhelfer/innen) are volunteers whose main task is counting the votes after polls close — they don't write official notifications or brief the media.

de.q: In Deutschland helfen ehrenamtliche Wahlhelferinnen und Wahlhelfer bei den Wahlen. Was ist eine Aufgabe von Wahlhelferinnen/Wahlhelfern?
o: Sie helfen Kindern und alten Menschen beim Wählen.
Sie schreiben Karten und Briefe mit der Angabe des Wahllokals.
Sie geben Zwischenergebnisse an Journalisten weiter.
Sie zählen die Stimmen nach dem Ende der Wahl.

en.q: In Germany, volunteer election workers help with the elections. What is one of the tasks of election workers?
o: They help children and elderly people to vote.
They write cards and letters stating the polling station.
They pass on interim results to journalists.
They count the votes after the election has ended.

explanation.en: Like other election helpers, their core job is counting votes once polling ends — not writing notifications or briefing journalists.

de.q: Für wie viele Jahre wird der Bundestag in Deutschland gewählt?

en.q: For how many years is the Bundestag in Germany elected?

explanation.en: The Bundestag's term (Legislaturperiode) is 4 years.

de.q: Bei einer Bundestagswahl in Deutschland darf jede/jeder wählen, die/der …
o: in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland wohnt und wählen möchte.
Bürgerin/Bürger der Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist und mindestens 18 Jahre alt ist.
seit mindestens 3 Jahren in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland lebt.
Bürgerin/Bürger der Bundesrepublik Deutschland ist und mindestens 21 Jahre alt ist.

en.q: In a federal election (Bundestagswahl) in Germany, anyone may vote who …
o: lives in the Federal Republic of Germany and wants to vote.
is a citizen of the Federal Republic of Germany and is at least 18 years old.
has been living in the Federal Republic of Germany for at least 3 years.
is a citizen of the Federal Republic of Germany and is at least 21 years old.

explanation.en: Only German citizens aged 18 or older may vote in Bundestag elections — residency alone is not sufficient.

de.q: Wie oft gibt es normalerweise Bundestagswahlen in Deutschland?

en.q: How often are federal elections (Bundestagswahlen) normally held in Germany?

explanation.en: Federal elections normally take place every four years, matching the Bundestag's term length.

de.q: Für wie viele Jahre wird der Bundestag in Deutschland gewählt?

en.q: For how many years is the Bundestag in Germany elected?

explanation.en: As with question 107, the Bundestag's term is 4 years.

de.q: Welche Handlungen mit Bezug auf den Staat Israel sind in Deutschland verboten?
o: das Aufhängen einer israelischen Flagge auf dem Privatgrundstück
eine Diskussion über die Politik Israels
der öffentliche Aufruf zur Vernichtung Israels

en.q: Which actions relating to the State of Israel are prohibited in Germany?
o: hanging an Israeli flag on private property
a public call for the destruction of Israel

explanation.en: Publicly calling for the destruction of Israel is a criminal offense in Germany. However, criticizing Israeli government policies, displaying Israeli flags, and discussing Israeli politics are all perfectly legal and protected by freedom of speech. The distinction is crucial: political criticism is allowed; calling for the elimination of a state is incitement and violates German law.

de.q: Die Wahlen in Deutschland sind …

en.q: Elections in Germany are …

explanation.en: German elections are secret (geheim) — one of the five key election principles (universal, direct, free, equal, secret).

de.q: Wahlen in Deutschland gewinnt die Partei, die …
o: die meisten Männer mehrheitlich gewählt haben.
die meisten Stimmen bei den Arbeiterinnen/Arbeitern bekommen hat.
die meisten Erststimmen für ihre Kanzlerkandidatin/ihren Kanzlerkandidaten erhalten hat.

en.q: Elections in Germany are won by the party that …
o: the majority of men have voted for.
has received the most votes among workers.
has received the most first votes (Erststimmen) for its candidate for chancellor.

explanation.en: The party (or coalition) with the most votes overall wins — not based on demographic subgroups or a specific vote type alone.

de.q: An demokratischen Wahlen in Deutschland teilzunehmen ist …

en.q: Taking part in democratic elections in Germany is …

explanation.en: Voting in Germany is a right (Recht), not a legal obligation — unlike in some countries with compulsory voting.

de.q: Was bedeutet "aktives Wahlrecht" in Deutschland?
o: Man muss zur Auszählung der Stimmen gehen.

en.q: What does the “active right to vote” (aktives Wahlrecht) mean in Germany?
o: You have to go and vote.
You have to go to the counting of the votes.

explanation.en: "Active voting right" (aktives Wahlrecht) means the right to vote — distinct from "passive voting right" (the right to stand as a candidate).

de.q: Wenn Sie bei einer Bundestagswahl in Deutschland wählen dürfen, heißt das …

en.q: If you are allowed to vote in a federal election (Bundestagswahl) in Germany, this is called …

explanation.en: The right to vote itself is called aktives Wahlrecht (active voting right).

de.q: Wie viel Prozent der Zweitstimmen müssen Parteien mindestens bekommen, um in den Deutschen Bundestag gewählt zu werden?

en.q: What is the minimum percentage of second votes (Zweitstimmen) that parties must receive in order to be elected to the German Bundestag?

explanation.en: The 5% threshold (5%-Hürde) requires parties to win at least 5% of second votes nationwide (or 3 direct constituency seats) to enter the Bundestag.

de.q: Wer darf bei den rund 40 jüdischen Makkabi-Sportvereinen Mitglied werden?

en.q: Who may become a member of the roughly 40 Jewish Maccabi sports clubs?

explanation.en: The Makkabi sports clubs (named after the ancient Jewish Maccabees) are open to EVERYONE, regardless of religion, nationality, or background. There are about 40 Makkabi clubs across Germany. This question emphasizes that Jewish institutions in Germany are inclusive and part of broader German society. Makkabi Deutschland is a member of the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB).

de.q: Wahlen in Deutschland sind frei. Was bedeutet das?
o: Alle verurteilten Straftäterinnen/Straftäter dürfen nicht wählen.
Wenn ich wählen gehen möchte, muss meine Arbeitgeberin/mein Arbeitgeber mir frei geben.
Jede Person kann ohne Zwang entscheiden, ob sie wählen möchte und wen sie wählen möchte.
Ich kann frei entscheiden, wo ich wählen gehen möchte.

en.q: Elections in Germany are free. What does that mean?
o: All convicted offenders are not allowed to vote.
If I want to go and vote, my employer has to give me time off.
Every person can decide without coercion whether they want to vote and whom they want to vote for.
I can freely decide where I want to go to vote.

explanation.en: "Free" elections mean voters decide without coercion whether to vote and for whom — not about polling location choice or employer obligations.

de.q: Das Wahlsystem in Deutschland ist ein …

en.q: The electoral system in Germany is …
o: a majority and proportional voting system.

explanation.en: Germany uses a mixed-member proportional system combining majority voting (Erststimme, direct constituency) and proportional representation (Zweitstimme, party lists).

de.q: Eine Partei möchte in den Deutschen Bundestag. Sie muss aber einen Mindestanteil an Wählerstimmen haben. Das heißt …

en.q: A party wants to get into the German Bundestag. But it must have a minimum share of the votes. This is called …

explanation.en: This minimum vote requirement is called the 5%-Hürde (5% threshold/hurdle).

de.q: Welchem Grundsatz unterliegen Wahlen in Deutschland? Wahlen in Deutschland sind …

en.q: Which principle are elections in Germany subject to? Elections in Germany are …

explanation.en: German elections follow five principles: universal, direct, free, equal, and secret — here shortened to free, equal, secret.

de.q: Was ist in Deutschland die "5%-Hürde"?
o: Abstimmungsregelung im Bundestag für kleine Parteien
Mindestanteil an Wählerstimmen, um ins Parlament zu kommen

en.q: What is the “5% hurdle” (5%-Hürde) in Germany?
o: voting rule in the Bundestag for small parties
attendance check in the Bundestag for votes
minimum share of the votes in order to get into parliament
attendance check in the Bundesrat for votes

explanation.en: The 5% threshold is the minimum share of votes (5%) a party needs nationwide to enter parliament.

de.q: Die Bundestagswahl in Deutschland ist die Wahl …

en.q: The federal election (Bundestagswahl) in Germany is the election …
o: of the parliaments of the federal states (Länder).

explanation.en: The Bundestagswahl elects Germany's national parliament (the Bundestag itself), not the Chancellor or President directly.

de.q: In einer Demokratie ist eine Funktion von regelmäßigen Wahlen, …
o: die Bürgerinnen und Bürger zu zwingen, ihre Stimme abzugeben.
nach dem Willen der Wählermehrheit den Wechsel der Regierung zu ermöglichen.
den Armen mehr Macht zu geben.

en.q: In a democracy, one function of regular elections is …
o: to force citizens to cast their vote.
to make a change of government possible in accordance with the will of the majority of voters.
to keep the laws existing in the country.
to give the poor more power.

explanation.en: Regular elections enable peaceful change of government based on voter majority will — a core democratic function.

de.q: Was bekommen wahlberechtigte Bürgerinnen und Bürger in Deutschland vor einer Wahl?
o: eine Wahlerlaubnis von der Bundespräsidentin/von dem Bundespräsidenten

en.q: What do citizens in Germany who are entitled to vote receive before an election?
o: a voter notification card from the municipality (Gemeinde)
a voting permit from the Federal President (Bundespräsident)
a notification from the Federal Convention (Bundesversammlung)
a notification from the parish office

explanation.en: Eligible voters receive a Wahlbenachrichtigung (voting notification) from their local municipality ahead of elections.

de.q: Warum gibt es die 5%-Hürde im Wahlgesetz der Bundesrepublik Deutschland? Es gibt sie, weil …
o: die Programme von vielen kleinen Parteien viele Gemeinsamkeiten haben.
die Bürgerinnen und Bürger bei vielen kleinen Parteien die Orientierung verlieren können.
viele kleine Parteien die Regierungsbildung erschweren.
die kleinen Parteien nicht so viel Geld haben, um die Politikerinnen und Politiker zu bezahlen.

en.q: Why is there a 5% hurdle (5%-Hürde) in the electoral law of the Federal Republic of Germany? It exists because …
o: the programs of many small parties have a lot in common.
citizens can lose their bearings when there are many small parties.
many small parties make it more difficult to form a government.
the small parties do not have that much money to pay the politicians.

explanation.en: The threshold exists to prevent excessive party fragmentation, which historically made forming stable governments difficult (as in the Weimar Republic).

de.q: Parlamentsmitglieder, die von den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern gewählt werden, nennt man …

en.q: Members of parliament who are elected by the citizens are called …

explanation.en: Elected members of parliament are called Abgeordnete (members/deputies).

de.q: Vom Volk gewählt wird in Deutschland …

en.q: In Germany, the people elect …
o: the Minister-President (Ministerpräsident) of a federal state.

explanation.en: Citizens directly elect the Bundestag; the Chancellor, Minister-Presidents, and Federal President are elected indirectly by other bodies.

de.q: Welcher Stimmzettel wäre bei einer Bundestagswahl gültig?

en.q: Which ballot paper would be valid in a federal election (Bundestagswahl)?

explanation.en: A valid ballot has exactly one mark in the first-vote column and one in the second-vote column — any other marking pattern invalidates the ballot.

de.q: In Deutschland ist eine Bürgermeisterin/ein Bürgermeister …

en.q: In Germany, a mayor is …

explanation.en: A Bürgermeister/in is the head of a municipality (Gemeinde) — not a school, bank, or political party.

de.q: Viele Menschen in Deutschland arbeiten in ihrer Freizeit ehrenamtlich. Was bedeutet das?
o: Sie arbeiten freiwillig und unbezahlt in Vereinen und Verbänden.
Sie arbeiten in einem Krankenhaus und verdienen dabei Geld.

en.q: Many people in Germany work in an honorary capacity (ehrenamtlich) in their free time. What does that mean?
o: They work voluntarily and unpaid in clubs and associations.
They work in the Federal Government (Bundesregierung).
They work in a hospital and earn money doing so.

explanation.en: Ehrenamtliche (voluntary) work means working unpaid in clubs, associations, or charities — a widespread and valued practice in German society.

de.q: Was ist bei Bundestags- und Landtagswahlen in Deutschland erlaubt?
o: Der Ehemann wählt für seine Frau mit.
Man kann durch Briefwahl seine Stimme abgeben.
Man kann am Wahltag telefonisch seine Stimme abgeben.
Kinder ab dem Alter von 14 Jahren dürfen wählen.

en.q: What is permitted in federal and state parliament elections (Bundestags- und Landtagswahlen) in Germany?
o: The husband also votes on behalf of his wife.
You can cast your vote by postal voting.
You can cast your vote by telephone on election day.
Children aged 14 and over are allowed to vote.

explanation.en: Postal voting (Briefwahl) is a legal and common way to vote in Germany — phone voting, proxy voting by a spouse, and voting under 18 are not allowed.

de.q: Man will die Buslinie abschaffen, mit der Sie immer zur Arbeit fahren. Was können Sie machen, um die Buslinie zu erhalten?
o: Ich beteilige mich an einer Bürgerinitiative für die Erhaltung der Buslinie oder gründe selber eine Initiative.
Ich werde Mitglied in einem Sportverein und trainiere Radfahren.
Ich wende mich an das Finanzamt, weil ich als Steuerzahlerin/Steuerzahler ein Recht auf die Buslinie habe.
Ich schreibe einen Brief an das Forstamt der Gemeinde.

en.q: There are plans to abolish the bus route you always take to work. What can you do to keep the bus route?
o: I take part in a citizens' initiative (Bürgerinitiative) to keep the bus route or start an initiative myself.
I join a sports club and train in cycling.
I contact the tax office (Finanzamt) because, as a taxpayer, I have a right to the bus route.
I write a letter to the municipal forestry office (Forstamt).

explanation.en: Joining or forming a citizens' initiative (Bürgerinitiative) is the recognized, effective way to advocate for local issues like public transit in Germany.

de.q: Wen vertreten die Gewerkschaften in Deutschland?

en.q: Whom do trade unions (Gewerkschaften) represent in Germany?

explanation.en: Trade unions represent employees (workers), negotiating on their behalf with employers — not businesses or the self-employed.

de.q: Sie gehen in Deutschland zum Arbeitsgericht bei …
o: ungerechtfertigter Kündigung durch Ihre Chefin/Ihren Chef.

en.q: In Germany, you go to the labor court (Arbeitsgericht) in the case of …
o: an incorrect statement of service charges (Nebenkostenabrechnung).

explanation.en: Labor courts (Arbeitsgerichte) handle employment disputes such as unjustified dismissal — not utility bills, neighbor disputes, or traffic accidents.

de.q: Welches Gericht ist in Deutschland bei Konflikten in der Arbeitswelt zuständig?

en.q: Which court in Germany is responsible for conflicts in the world of work?

explanation.en: The Arbeitsgericht (labor court) handles workplace and employment-related conflicts specifically.

de.q: Was kann ich in Deutschland machen, wenn mir meine Arbeitgeberin/mein Arbeitgeber zu Unrecht gekündigt hat?
o: weiterarbeiten und freundlich zur Chefin/zum Chef sein
ein Mahnverfahren gegen die Arbeitgeberin/den Arbeitgeber führen
die Arbeitgeberin/den Arbeitgeber bei der Polizei anzeigen

en.q: What can I do in Germany if my employer has wrongfully dismissed me?
o: keep working and be friendly to the boss
initiate payment-order proceedings (Mahnverfahren) against the employer
file an action for protection against dismissal (Kündigungsschutzklage)
report the employer to the police

explanation.en: The correct legal remedy is a Kündigungsschutzklage (wrongful dismissal lawsuit) filed at the labor court — not a police report or debt claim.

de.q: Wann kommt es in Deutschland zu einem Prozess vor Gericht? Wenn jemand …
o: eine Straftat begangen hat und angeklagt wird.
eine andere Meinung als die der Regierung vertritt.
sein Auto falsch geparkt hat und es abgeschleppt wird.

en.q: When does a case go to trial in court in Germany? When someone …
o: has committed a criminal offense and is charged.
holds an opinion different from that of the government.
has parked their car incorrectly and it is towed away.

explanation.en: A criminal trial occurs when someone commits and is charged with a crime — not for religious conversion, differing political opinions, or parking violations.

de.q: Was macht eine Schöffin/ein Schöffe in Deutschland? Sie/Er …
o: entscheidet mit Richterinnen/Richtern über Schuld und Strafe.

en.q: What does a lay assessor (Schöffe) do in Germany? They …
o: decide on guilt and punishment together with judges.

explanation.en: A Schöffe/in (lay judge) is a citizen volunteer who sits alongside professional judges and votes on guilt and sentencing — not a legal advisor or defense attorney.

de.q: Wer berät in Deutschland Personen bei Rechtsfragen und vertritt sie vor Gericht?

en.q: In Germany, who advises people on legal questions and represents them in court?

explanation.en: A Rechtsanwalt/in (lawyer) advises clients and represents them legally — judges, lay judges, and prosecutors have different, impartial roles in court.

de.q: Was ist die Hauptaufgabe einer Richterin/eines Richters in Deutschland? Eine Richterin/ein Richter …
o: vertritt Bürgerinnen und Bürger vor einem Gericht.
arbeitet an einem Gericht und spricht Urteile.

en.q: What is the main task of a judge in Germany? A judge …
o: works at a court and pronounces judgments.
looks after young people in court.

explanation.en: A judge's main role is to work at a court and deliver rulings/verdicts — not to represent citizens, change laws, or act as a youth caseworker.

de.q: Eine Richterin/ein Richter in Deutschland gehört zur …

en.q: In Germany, a judge belongs to the …

explanation.en: Judges belong to the Judikative (judiciary), the third branch of state power alongside the executive and legislature.

de.q: Eine Richterin/ein Richter gehört in Deutschland zur …

en.q: In Germany, a judge belongs to the …

explanation.en: Judges belong to the rechtsprechende Gewalt (judicial power) — the power to interpret and apply the law.

de.q: In Deutschland wird die Staatsgewalt geteilt. Für welche Staatsgewalt arbeitet eine Richterin/ein Richter? Für die …

en.q: In Germany, state power is divided. For which branch of state power does a judge work? For the …

explanation.en: Judges belong to the Judikative (judiciary), the branch of state power responsible for interpreting and applying the law — distinct from the executive, legislature, or the press, which is not a branch of state power at all.

de.q: Wie nennt man in Deutschland ein Verfahren vor einem Gericht?

en.q: In Germany, what are proceedings before a court called?

explanation.en: A court proceeding is called a Prozess (trial/legal proceeding) in German.

de.q: Was ist die Arbeit einer Richterin/eines Richters in Deutschland?

en.q: What is the work of a judge in Germany?

explanation.en: A judge's work is Recht sprechen — delivering rulings/administering justice, not governing or legislating.

de.q: Was ist eine Aufgabe der Polizei in Deutschland?
o: die Einhaltung von Gesetzen zu überwachen

en.q: What is one of the tasks of the police in Germany?

explanation.en: Policing law compliance is the police's core task — defending the country is the military's job, and passing laws is parliament's.

de.q: Was ist ein Beispiel für antisemitisches Verhalten?

en.q: What is an example of antisemitic behavior?

explanation.en: Denying the Holocaust is a clear example of antisemitic behavior and is a criminal offense in Germany.
