Important distinctions: visiting Jewish festivals, criticizing Israeli government policies, and playing sports with or against Jewish people are all normal, acceptable activities. Criticism of Israeli government policy is NOT antisemitism. However, denying the systematic murder of 6 million Jews is both antisemitic and illegal.

de.q: Eine Gerichtsschöffin/ein Gerichtsschöffe in Deutschland ist …
o: eine Person, die Jura studiert hat.

en.q: In Germany, a court lay assessor (Gerichtsschöffe) is …
o: the deputy of the head of the city.
a member of a municipal council (Gemeinderat).
a person who has studied law.

explanation.en: A Gerichtsschöffe/in is a volunteer, honorary lay judge — no law degree is required, unlike professional judges.

de.q: Wer baute die Mauer in Berlin?

en.q: Who built the Wall in Berlin?

explanation.en: The GDR (East Germany) built the Berlin Wall in 1961 to stop mass emigration to the West.

de.q: Wann waren die Nationalsozialisten mit Adolf Hitler in Deutschland an der Macht?

en.q: When were the National Socialists under Adolf Hitler in power in Germany?

explanation.en: The Nazi regime held power from 1933 (Hitler's appointment as Chancellor) to 1945 (Germany's defeat in WWII).

de.q: Was war am 8. Mai 1945?
o: Wahl von Konrad Adenauer zum Bundeskanzler
Ende des Zweiten Weltkriegs in Europa

en.q: What happened on May 8, 1945?
o: Start of the construction of the Berlin Wall
Election of Konrad Adenauer as Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler)
End of the Second World War in Europe

explanation.en: May 8, 1945 marks Germany's unconditional surrender, ending World War II in Europe.

de.q: Wann war der Zweite Weltkrieg zu Ende?

en.q: When did the Second World War end?

explanation.en: World War II ended in 1945.

de.q: Wann waren die Nationalsozialisten in Deutschland an der Macht?

en.q: When were the National Socialists in power in Germany?

explanation.en: The Nazi regime governed Germany from 1933 to 1945.

de.q: In welchem Jahr wurde Hitler Reichskanzler?

en.q: In which year did Hitler become Reich Chancellor (Reichskanzler)?

explanation.en: Hitler became Reich Chancellor in 1933, appointed by President Hindenburg.

de.q: Die Nationalsozialisten mit Adolf Hitler errichteten 1933 in Deutschland …

en.q: In 1933, the National Socialists under Adolf Hitler established in Germany …

explanation.en: The Nazis established a dictatorship, abolishing democratic institutions and civil liberties.

de.q: Das "Dritte Reich" war eine …

en.q: The “Third Reich” was a …

explanation.en: The "Third Reich" (Nazi Germany, 1933-1945) was a dictatorship under Hitler.

de.q: Was gab es in Deutschland nicht während der Zeit des Nationalsozialismus?

en.q: What did not exist in Germany during the era of National Socialism?

explanation.en: Free elections did NOT exist under Nazi rule — censorship, arbitrary arrests, and persecution were widespread instead.

de.q: Welcher Krieg dauerte von 1939 bis 1945?

en.q: Which war lasted from 1939 to 1945?

explanation.en: World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945.

de.q: Was kennzeichnete den NS-Staat? Eine Politik …

en.q: What characterized the Nazi state (NS-Staat)? A policy …

explanation.en: State racism was a defining feature of the Nazi regime, underpinning its persecution policies — the opposite of free speech, religious freedom, or democracy.

de.q: Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg wurde bekannt durch …
o: eine Goldmedaille bei den Olympischen Spielen 1936.
das Attentat auf Hitler am 20. Juli 1944.

en.q: Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg became known for …
o: a gold medal at the 1936 Olympic Games.
the construction of the Reichstag building.
the assassination attempt on Hitler on July 20, 1944.

explanation.en: Stauffenberg led the failed July 20, 1944 assassination attempt on Hitler, a key act of German resistance to Nazism.

de.q: In welchem Jahr zerstörten die Nationalsozialisten Synagogen und jüdische Geschäfte in Deutschland?

en.q: In which year did the National Socialists destroy synagogues and Jewish shops in Germany?

explanation.en: The Nazis destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany in 1938, during the November Pogrom (Kristallnacht) on November 9, 1938.

de.q: Was passierte am 9. November 1938 in Deutschland?
o: Mit dem Angriff auf Polen beginnt der Zweite Weltkrieg.
Die Nationalsozialisten verlieren eine Wahl und lösen den Reichstag auf.
Jüdische Geschäfte und Synagogen werden durch Nationalsozialisten und ihre Anhänger zerstört.
Hitler wird Reichspräsident und lässt alle Parteien verbieten.

en.q: What happened in Germany on November 9, 1938?
o: The Second World War begins with the attack on Poland.
The National Socialists lose an election and dissolve the Reichstag.
Jewish shops and synagogues are destroyed by National Socialists and their supporters.
Hitler becomes Reich President (Reichspräsident) and has all parties banned.

explanation.en: November 9, 1938 was the November Pogrom ("Kristallnacht"), when Nazis and supporters destroyed Jewish synagogues and businesses across Germany.

de.q: Wie hieß der erste Bundeskanzler der Bundesrepublik Deutschland?

en.q: What was the name of the first Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) of the Federal Republic of Germany?

explanation.en: Konrad Adenauer was the first Federal Chancellor of West Germany, serving from 1949 to 1963.

de.q: Bei welchen Demonstrationen in Deutschland riefen die Menschen "Wir sind das Volk"?
o: bei den Demonstrationen 1968 in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland
bei den Anti-Atomkraft-Demonstrationen 1985 in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland
bei den Montagsdemonstrationen 1989 in der DDR

en.q: At which demonstrations in Germany did people chant “We are the people” (Wir sind das Volk)?
o: at the 1953 workers' uprising in the GDR (DDR)
at the 1968 demonstrations in the Federal Republic of Germany
at the 1985 anti-nuclear power demonstrations in the Federal Republic of Germany
at the 1989 Monday demonstrations in the GDR (DDR)

explanation.en: The 1989 Monday demonstrations (Montagsdemonstrationen) in the GDR, especially in Leipzig, were key to the Peaceful Revolution that led to the Wall's fall.

de.q: Welche Länder wurden nach dem Zweiten Weltkrieg in Deutschland als "Alliierte Besatzungsmächte" bezeichnet?

en.q: Which countries were referred to in Germany after the Second World War as “Allied occupying powers” (Alliierte Besatzungsmächte)?
o: Soviet Union, Great Britain, Poland, Sweden
USA, Soviet Union, Great Britain, France

explanation.en: The four Allied occupying powers were the USA, Soviet Union, Great Britain, and France, each administering a zone of postwar Germany.

de.q: Welches Land war keine "Alliierte Besatzungsmacht" in Deutschland?

en.q: Which country was not an “Allied occupying power” (Alliierte Besatzungsmacht) in Germany?

explanation.en: Japan was not one of the four occupying powers in Germany — it was itself occupied separately after WWII.

de.q: Wann wurde die Bundesrepublik Deutschland gegründet?

en.q: When was the Federal Republic of Germany founded?

explanation.en: The Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) was founded in 1949.

de.q: Was gab es während der Zeit des Nationalsozialismus in Deutschland?
o: das Recht zur freien Entfaltung der Persönlichkeit

en.q: What existed in Germany during the era of National Socialism?
o: the right to free development of one's personality

explanation.en: The Nazi regime banned all political parties except the NSDAP — the opposite of personal freedoms, press freedom, or human dignity protections.

de.q: Soziale Marktwirtschaft bedeutet, die Wirtschaft …
o: steuert sich allein nach Angebot und Nachfrage.
wird vom Staat geplant und gesteuert, Angebot und Nachfrage werden nicht berücksichtigt.
richtet sich nach der Nachfrage im Ausland.
richtet sich nach Angebot und Nachfrage, aber der Staat sorgt für einen sozialen Ausgleich.

en.q: Social market economy (soziale Marktwirtschaft) means that the economy …
o: is regulated solely by supply and demand.
is planned and controlled by the state; supply and demand are not taken into account.
is guided by supply and demand, but the state ensures social balance.

Anne (13 years old) and Tim (25 years old)

explanation.en: Anne is only 13, below the legal age of consent and marriage in Germany, so she may not live together as a couple with Tim — unlike the other pairs, who are all adults.

de.q: Ab welchem Alter ist man in Deutschland volljährig?

en.q: From what age are you legally an adult in Germany?

explanation.en: In Germany, a person reaches legal adulthood (Volljährigkeit) at age 18, gaining full legal rights and responsibilities.

de.q: Eine Frau ist schwanger. Sie ist kurz vor und nach der Geburt ihres Kindes vom Gesetz besonders beschützt. Wie heißt dieser Schutz?

en.q: A woman is pregnant. Shortly before and after the birth of her child she is specially protected by law. What is this protection called?

explanation.en: Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection) provides at least 8 weeks off after birth (12 for multiple/premature births) — distinct from Elternzeit (parental leave), which can be much longer.

de.q: Die Erziehung der Kinder ist in Deutschland vor allem Aufgabe …

en.q: In Germany, raising children is above all the task …

explanation.en: As with question 242, raising children is primarily the parents' responsibility under German law.

de.q: Wer ist in Deutschland hauptsächlich verantwortlich für die Kindererziehung?

en.q: Who in Germany is mainly responsible for raising children?

explanation.en: Parents hold the primary responsibility for raising their children in Germany.

de.q: In Deutschland hat man die besten Chancen auf einen gut bezahlten Arbeitsplatz, wenn man …

en.q: In Germany you have the best chances of getting a well-paid job if you …
o: are a member of a party.

explanation.en: Good education/qualifications are the key factor for job prospects in Germany, not religion, gender, or party membership.

de.q: Wenn man in Deutschland ein Kind schlägt, …
o: geht das nur die Familie etwas an.
kann man dafür nicht bestraft werden.

en.q: If you hit a child in Germany, …
o: it is only the family's business.
you cannot be punished for it.
you can be punished for it.

explanation.en: Since 2000, children in Germany have a legal right to a nonviolent upbringing — hitting a child is punishable, not a private family matter.

de.q: In Deutschland …
o: darf man zur gleichen Zeit nur mit einer Partnerin/einem Partner verheiratet sein.
kann man mehrere Ehepartnerinnen/Ehepartner gleichzeitig haben.
darf man nicht wieder heiraten, wenn man einmal verheiratet war.
darf eine Frau nicht wieder heiraten, wenn ihr Mann gestorben ist.

en.q: In Germany …
o: you may be married to only one partner at a time.
you can have several spouses at the same time.
you may not marry again once you have been married.
a woman may not marry again if her husband has died.

explanation.en: Germany practices monogamy — one may only be married to one person at a time; remarriage after divorce or widowhood is fully permitted.

de.q: Wo müssen Sie sich anmelden, wenn Sie in Deutschland umziehen?

en.q: Where do you have to register when you move house in Germany?

explanation.en: You must register your new address at the Einwohnermeldeamt (residents' registration office) whenever you move.

de.q: In Deutschland dürfen Ehepaare sich scheiden lassen. Meistens müssen sie dazu das "Trennungsjahr" einhalten. Was bedeutet das?
o: Die Ehegatten sind ein Jahr verheiratet, dann ist die Scheidung möglich.
Das Besuchsrecht für die Kinder gilt ein Jahr.
Die Ehegatten führen mindestens ein Jahr getrennt ihr eigenes Leben. Danach ist die Scheidung möglich.

en.q: In Germany, married couples are allowed to get divorced. In most cases they have to observe the “year of separation” (Trennungsjahr) to do so. What does that mean?
o: The divorce proceedings take one year.
The spouses are married for one year, and then a divorce is possible.
The visiting rights for the children apply for one year.
The spouses live their own lives separately for at least one year. After that, a divorce is possible.

explanation.en: German law requires a minimum one-year separation period (Trennungsjahr) before a divorce can be finalized, demonstrating the marriage is irreparably broken.

de.q: Bei Erziehungsproblemen können Eltern in Deutschland Hilfe erhalten vom …

en.q: In Germany, parents with problems raising their children can get help from the …

explanation.en: The Jugendamt (youth welfare office) is responsible for protecting children from abuse and neglect.

de.q: Ein Ehepaar möchte in Deutschland ein Restaurant eröffnen. Was braucht es dazu unbedingt?
o: eine Gaststättenerlaubnis von der zuständigen Behörde

en.q: A married couple wants to open a restaurant in Germany. What do they absolutely need for this?
o: approval from the residents' registration office (Einwohnermeldeamt)
a restaurant license (Gaststättenerlaubnis) from the responsible authority

explanation.en: Opening a restaurant/pub (Gaststätte) requires a Gaststättenerlaubnis from the relevant authority — not police, party, or residents' office approval.

de.q: Eine erwachsene Frau möchte in Deutschland das Abitur nachholen. Das kann sie an …

en.q: An adult woman in Germany wants to obtain the Abitur that she did not get at school. She can do this at …

explanation.en: An Abendgymnasium (evening high school) allows working adults to obtain the Abitur later in life.

de.q: Was darf das Jugendamt in Deutschland?
o: Es entscheidet, welche Schule das Kind besucht.
Es kann ein Kind, das geschlagen wird oder hungern muss, aus der Familie nehmen.
Es bezahlt das Kindergeld an die Eltern.
Es kontrolliert, ob das Kind einen Kindergarten besucht.

en.q: What is the youth welfare office (Jugendamt) allowed to do in Germany?
o: It decides which school the child attends.
It can remove a child who is beaten or has to go hungry from the family.
It pays child benefit (Kindergeld) to the parents.
It checks whether the child attends a kindergarten.

explanation.en: In severe cases of abuse or neglect, the Jugendamt can remove a child from the family to protect their safety and wellbeing.

de.q: Das Berufsinformationszentrum BIZ bei der Bundesagentur für Arbeit in Deutschland hilft bei der …

en.q: The career information center BIZ (Berufsinformationszentrum) at the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) in Germany helps with …

explanation.en: The BIZ helps people, especially young people, find apprenticeships and explore career options.

de.q: In Deutschland hat ein Kind in der Schule …

en.q: In Germany, a child at school has …
o: a right to unlimited free time.

explanation.en: Schulpflicht (compulsory schooling) means mandatory attendance — not a right to free time, subject choice, or fee entitlement.

de.q: Ein Mann möchte mit 30 Jahren in Deutschland sein Abitur nachholen. Wo kann er das tun? An …

en.q: A 30-year-old man in Germany wants to obtain the Abitur that he did not get at school. Where can he do this? At …

explanation.en: As with question 257, an Abendgymnasium allows working adults, including those with prior vocational training, to earn the Abitur.

de.q: Was bedeutet in Deutschland der Grundsatz der Gleichbehandlung?
o: Niemand darf z.B. wegen einer Behinderung benachteiligt werden.
Man darf andere Personen benachteiligen, wenn ausreichende persönliche Gründe hierfür vorliegen.
Niemand darf gegen Personen klagen, wenn sie benachteiligt wurden.
Es ist für alle Gesetz, benachteiligten Gruppen jährlich Geld zu spenden.

en.q: What does the principle of equal treatment mean in Germany?
o: No one may be disadvantaged, e.g. because of a disability.
You may disadvantage other people if there are sufficient personal reasons for doing so.
No one may take legal action against people if they have been disadvantaged.
It is the law for everyone to donate money to disadvantaged groups every year.

explanation.en: The Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz (General Equal Treatment Act) prohibits disadvantaging people based on protected characteristics like disability, race, gender, or religion.

de.q: In Deutschland sind Jugendliche ab 14 Jahren strafmündig. Das bedeutet: Jugendliche, die 14 Jahre und älter sind und gegen Strafgesetze verstoßen, …
o: teilen die Strafe mit ihren Eltern.

en.q: In Germany, young people aged 14 and over are criminally responsible (strafmündig). This means: young people who are 14 or older and break criminal laws …
o: share the punishment with their parents.

explanation.en: From age 14, young people are criminally responsible (strafmündig) in Germany and can be punished — though under separate juvenile law, not treated exactly like adults.

de.q: Zu welchem Fest tragen Menschen in Deutschland bunte Kostüme und Masken?

en.q: At which festival do people in Germany wear colorful costumes and masks?

explanation.en: Rosenmontag (Rose Monday) is the peak celebration day of Carnival (Karneval/Fasching), especially in the Rhineland, featuring parades and costumes.

de.q: Wohin muss man in Deutschland zuerst gehen, wenn man heiraten möchte?

en.q: Where do you have to go first in Germany if you want to get married?
o: to the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit)

explanation.en: A newborn's birth is registered at the Standesamt (civil registry office), the same office that handles marriages.

de.q: Wann beginnt die gesetzliche Nachtruhe in Deutschland?

en.q: When does the legally required nighttime quiet period (Nachtruhe) begin in Germany?
o: when the neighbors go to bed

explanation.en: Nighttime quiet hours (Nachtruhe) typically begin at 10 PM in Germany, a common standard in local noise regulations.

de.q: Eine junge Frau in Deutschland, 22 Jahre alt, lebt mit ihrem Freund zusammen. Die Eltern der Frau finden das nicht gut, weil ihnen der Freund nicht gefällt. Was können die Eltern tun?
o: Sie müssen die Entscheidung der volljährigen Tochter respektieren.
Sie haben das Recht, die Tochter in die elterliche Wohnung zurückzuholen.
Sie können zur Polizei gehen und die Tochter anzeigen.
Sie suchen einen anderen Mann für die Tochter.

en.q: A young woman in Germany, 22 years old, lives with her boyfriend. The woman's parents don't approve because they don't like the boyfriend. What can the parents do?
o: They must respect the decision of their adult daughter.
They have the right to bring the daughter back to the parental home.
They can go to the police and report the daughter.
They look for another man for the daughter.

explanation.en: At 19, she is a legal adult and free to make her own decisions, including where to live — parents cannot legally force her to stay.

de.q: Eine junge Frau will den Führerschein machen. Sie hat Angst vor der Prüfung, weil ihre Muttersprache nicht Deutsch ist. Was ist richtig?
o: Sie muss mindestens zehn Jahre in Deutschland leben, bevor sie den Führerschein machen kann.
Wenn sie kein Deutsch kann, darf sie keinen Führerschein haben.
Sie muss den Führerschein in dem Land machen, in dem man ihre Sprache spricht.
Sie kann die Theorie-Prüfung vielleicht in ihrer Muttersprache machen. Es gibt mehr als zehn Sprachen zur Auswahl.

en.q: A young woman wants to get her driver's license. She is afraid of the test because her native language is not German. What is correct?
o: She has to live in Germany for at least ten years before she can get a driver's license.
If she does not speak German, she is not allowed to have a driver's license.
She has to get her driver's license in a country where her language is spoken.
She may be able to take the theory test in her native language. There are more than ten languages to choose from.

explanation.en: Germany's driving theory test is available in multiple languages (more than ten), allowing non-German speakers to take it in their native tongue.

de.q: In Deutschland haben Kinder ab dem Alter von drei Jahren bis zur Ersteinschulung einen Anspruch auf …

en.q: In Germany, children from the age of three until they start school are entitled to …
o: a place in a sports club.

explanation.en: Children in Germany have a legal right to a kindergarten place from age three until they start school.

de.q: Die Volkshochschule in Deutschland ist eine Einrichtung …

en.q: The community education center (Volkshochschule) in Germany is an institution …

explanation.en: The Volkshochschule (VHS) offers affordable adult continuing education courses — languages, integration courses, hobbies — open to all ages.

de.q: Was ist in Deutschland ein Brauch zu Weihnachten?
o: sich mit Masken und Kostümen verkleiden

en.q: What is a Christmas custom in Germany?
o: dressing up in masks and costumes
putting pumpkins in front of the door

explanation.en: Decorating a fir tree (Tannenbaum) is a classic German Christmas tradition.

de.q: Welche Lebensform ist in Deutschland nicht erlaubt?
o: Mann und Frau sind geschieden und leben mit neuen Partnern zusammen.
Ein alleinerziehender Vater lebt mit seinen zwei Kindern zusammen.
Ein Mann ist mit zwei Frauen zur selben Zeit verheiratet.

en.q: Which way of living together is not allowed in Germany?
o: A husband and wife are divorced and live with new partners.
A single father lives with his two children.
A man is married to two women at the same time.

explanation.en: Germany practices monogamy — being married to two people at once (polygamy) is not legally allowed, unlike the other listed living arrangements which are all legal.

de.q: Bei Erziehungsproblemen gehen Sie in Deutschland …

en.q: If you have problems raising your children in Germany, you go …

explanation.en: For parenting or child-rearing problems, the Jugendamt (youth welfare office) is the responsible authority in Germany — not a doctor, health office, or residents' office.

de.q: Sie haben in Deutschland absichtlich einen Brief geöffnet, der an eine andere Person adressiert ist. Was haben Sie nicht beachtet?

en.q: In Germany, you have deliberately opened a letter that is addressed to another person. What have you not respected?

explanation.en: The Briefgeheimnis (confidentiality of correspondence) protects private letters, emails, and communications from being read by others without permission.

de.q: Was braucht man in Deutschland für eine Ehescheidung?

en.q: What do you need in Germany to get a divorce?

explanation.en: A divorce in Germany requires a lawyer, since only a lawyer can file the divorce petition with the family court.

de.q: Was sollten Sie tun, wenn Sie von Ihrer Ansprechpartnerin/Ihrem Ansprechpartner in einer deutschen Behörde schlecht behandelt werden?
o: Ich muss mir diese Behandlung gefallen lassen.
Ich kann mich bei der Behördenleiterin/beim Behördenleiter beschweren.

en.q: What should you do if you are treated badly by your contact person at a German public authority?
o: I have to put up with this treatment.
I can complain to the head of the authority.

explanation.en: The proper channel is to lodge a formal complaint with the head of the relevant authority — not to threaten or simply accept unfair treatment.

de.q: Eine Frau, die ein zweijähriges Kind hat, bewirbt sich in Deutschland um eine Stelle. Was ist ein Beispiel für Diskriminierung? Sie bekommt die Stelle nur deshalb nicht, weil sie …
o: keine Erfahrungen in diesem Beruf hat.

en.q: A woman who has a two-year-old child applies for a job in Germany. What is an example of discrimination? She does not get the job only because she …
o: has salary expectations that are too high.
has no experience in this profession.

explanation.en: Germany's General Equal Treatment Act (Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz, AGG) prohibits discrimination based on gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, age, or sexual identity. Refusing a job applicant because she is a mother is gender discrimination — it is illegal regardless of the employer's reasons. The correct answer is that she is a mother (Option D).

de.q: Ein Mann im Rollstuhl hat sich auf eine Stelle als Buchhalter beworben. Was ist ein Beispiel für Diskriminierung? Er bekommt die Stelle nur deshalb nicht, weil er …

en.q: A man in a wheelchair has applied for a job as an accountant. What is an example of discrimination? He does not get the job only because he …
o: has salary expectations that are too high.

explanation.en: Rejecting a qualified applicant solely because they use a wheelchair is disability discrimination under the AGG. Disability is an irrelevant factor for an office-based accounting role. The other options — lack of experience, salary expectations, language skills — could be legitimate hiring criteria. Only using a wheelchair (Option A) constitutes discrimination.

de.q: In den meisten Mietshäusern in Deutschland gibt es eine "Hausordnung". Was steht in einer solchen "Hausordnung"? Sie nennt …
o: Regeln für die Benutzung öffentlicher Verkehrsmittel.
alle Mieterinnen und Mieter im Haus.
Regeln, an die sich alle Bewohnerinnen und Bewohner halten müssen.

en.q: In most rental apartment buildings in Germany there are “house rules” (Hausordnung). What is in such “house rules”? They list …
o: all the tenants in the building.
rules that all residents must follow.
the address of the nearest public order office (Ordnungsamt).

explanation.en: A Hausordnung is a set of rules that applies to all residents of an apartment building. It typically covers quiet hours (Ruhezeiten), use of shared spaces (stairwell, laundry room, courtyard), rubbish disposal, and general conduct. It is usually attached to the rental contract (Mietvertrag). Violations can lead to warnings (Abmahnung) or, in serious cases, termination of the tenancy.

de.q: Wenn Sie sich in Deutschland gegen einen falschen Steuerbescheid wehren wollen, müssen Sie …
o: warten, bis ein anderer Bescheid kommt.

en.q: If you want to challenge an incorrect tax assessment notice (Steuerbescheid) in Germany, you have to …
o: wait until a different notice arrives.

explanation.en: If you receive a Steuerbescheid (tax assessment notice) that you believe is incorrect, you must formally lodge an Einspruch (objection) with the Finanzamt (tax office) within one month of receiving the notice. If the Einspruch is rejected, you can take the matter to the Finanzgericht (tax court). Simply ignoring or discarding the notice is not a legal remedy and may result in the incorrect amount becoming legally binding.

de.q: Zwei Freunde wollen in ein öffentliches Schwimmbad in Deutschland. Beide haben eine dunkle Hautfarbe und werden deshalb nicht hineingelassen. Welches Recht wird in dieser Situation verletzt? Das Recht auf …

en.q: Two friends want to go to a public swimming pool in Germany. Both have dark skin and are not let in for that reason. Which right is being violated in this situation? The right to …

explanation.en: Refusing entry to a public facility based on skin colour is racial discrimination, violating the right to Gleichbehandlung (equal treatment) guaranteed by Article 3 of the Basic Law and reinforced by the AGG. Public facilities open to everyone must not discriminate. The other rights listed — freedom of opinion, assembly, and movement — are not relevant to this situation.

de.q: Welches Ehrenamt müssen deutsche Staatsbürgerinnen und Staatsbürger übernehmen, wenn sie dazu aufgefordert werden?

en.q: Which honorary office (Ehrenamt) must German citizens take on if they are called upon to do so?

explanation.en: In Germany, citizens can be legally required to serve as Wahlhelfer (polling station workers) during elections. This is one of the few civic duties that can be compelled — similar to jury service in other countries. Wahlhelfer help run the polling station, distribute ballots, and count votes. The duty is part of democratic participation. Other roles like coaching, library work, or teaching cannot be legally compelled.

de.q: Was tun Sie, wenn Sie eine falsche Rechnung von einer deutschen Behörde bekommen?
o: Ich lege Widerspruch bei der Behörde ein.
Ich schicke die Rechnung an die Behörde zurück.
Ich gehe mit der Rechnung zum Finanzamt.

en.q: What do you do if you receive an incorrect bill from a German public authority?
o: I leave the bill lying around.
I lodge an objection (Widerspruch) with the authority.
I send the bill back to the authority.
I take the bill to the tax office (Finanzamt).

explanation.en: When you receive an incorrect bill or administrative decision from a German authority, the correct legal step is to lodge a Widerspruch (formal objection). This must typically be done in writing within one month. Simply returning the document or ignoring it is not sufficient and the incorrect charge could become legally enforceable. The Widerspruch triggers a review process within the authority.

de.q: Was man für die Arbeit können muss, ändert sich in Zukunft sehr schnell. Was kann man tun?
o: Es ist egal, was man lernt.
Erwachsene müssen auch nach der Ausbildung immer weiter lernen.
Kinder lernen in der Schule alles, was im Beruf wichtig ist. Nach der Schule muss man nicht weiter lernen.
Alle müssen früher aufhören zu arbeiten, weil sich alles ändert.

en.q: What you need to be able to do for work is going to change very quickly in the future. What can you do?
o: It doesn't matter what you learn.
Adults must also keep learning after their vocational training.
At school, children learn everything that is important for their job. After school you don't have to keep learning.
Everyone has to stop working earlier because everything is changing.

explanation.en: In a rapidly changing economy and job market, lifelong learning (lebenslanges Lernen) is essential. Germany has a strong tradition of continuing education (Weiterbildung) and vocational training. Adults are expected to update their skills throughout their careers through further training, courses, and qualification programmes. This concept is reinforced by Germany's dual education system and extensive adult education institutions (Volkshochschulen).

de.q: Frau Frost arbeitet als fest angestellte Mitarbeiterin in einem Büro. Was muss sie nicht von ihrem Gehalt bezahlen?

en.q: Ms. Frost works as a permanent employee in an office. What does she not have to pay out of her salary?

explanation.en: As a salaried employee in Germany, Ms Frost must pay Lohnsteuer (income tax withheld at source), as well as social insurance contributions: Krankenversicherung (health), Rentenversicherung (pension), Pflegeversicherung (care), and Arbeitslosenversicherung (unemployment). However, she does not pay Umsatzsteuer (VAT / value-added tax) from her salary — VAT is paid by businesses on goods and services, not by employees from their wages.

de.q: Welche Organisation in einer Firma hilft den Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmern bei Problemen mit der Arbeitgeberin/dem Arbeitgeber?

en.q: Which body in a company helps employees with problems with their employer?

explanation.en: The Betriebsrat (works council) is an elected body that represents the interests of employees in companies with five or more staff. It has co-determination rights (Mitbestimmungsrechte) on matters such as working hours, holiday schedules, redundancies, and workplace safety. Employees can approach the Betriebsrat with disputes or grievances about their employer. The Betriebsrat is legally protected and independent of management.

de.q: Sie möchten bei einer Firma in Deutschland ihr Arbeitsverhältnis beenden. Was müssen Sie beachten?

en.q: You want to end your employment with a company in Germany. What do you have to observe?

explanation.en: In Germany, when an employee wishes to resign (kündigen), they must observe the Kündigungsfrist (notice period). The statutory minimum notice period for employees is four weeks (to the 15th or end of the month). Longer notice periods may apply depending on the employment contract or collective agreement (Tarifvertrag). Failing to observe the notice period can result in legal claims for damages. The resignation must generally be submitted in writing (Schriftform).

de.q: Woraus begründet sich Deutschlands besondere Verantwortung für Israel?
o: aus der Mitgliedschaft in der Europäischen Union (EU)
aus den nationalsozialistischen Verbrechen gegen Juden
aus dem Grundgesetz der Bundesrepublik Deutschland

en.q: What is Germany's special responsibility towards Israel based on?
o: on its membership in the European Union (EU)
on the National Socialist crimes against Jews
on the Basic Law (Grundgesetz) of the Federal Republic of Germany

explanation.en: Germany's special responsibility toward Israel stems from the Nazi crimes committed against Jews during the Holocaust — not from EU membership, the Basic Law, or Christian tradition.

de.q: Ein Mann mit dunkler Hautfarbe bewirbt sich um eine Stelle als Kellner in einem Restaurant in Deutschland. Was ist ein Beispiel für Diskriminierung? Er bekommt die Stelle nur deshalb nicht, weil …
o: er keine Erfahrungen im Beruf hat.

en.q: A man with dark skin applies for a job as a waiter in a restaurant in Germany. What is an example of discrimination? He does not get the job only because …
o: his knowledge of German is too limited.
he has salary expectations that are too high.
he has no experience in the profession.

explanation.en: Refusing to hire someone because of their skin colour is racial discrimination, prohibited under Germany's AGG (General Equal Treatment Act). The colour of skin is entirely irrelevant to the ability to work as a waiter. The other options — insufficient German, high salary expectations, lack of experience — could be legitimate factors in a hiring decision. Only rejecting someone because of their skin colour (Option C) is discrimination.

de.q: Sie haben in Deutschland einen Fernseher gekauft. Zu Hause packen Sie den Fernseher aus, doch er funktioniert nicht. Der Fernseher ist kaputt. Was können Sie machen?

en.q: You have bought a television in Germany. At home you unpack the television, but it doesn't work. The television is broken. What can you do?
o: make a complaint about the television (reklamieren)

explanation.en: In Germany, if you buy a defective product, you have the right to Gewährleistung (statutory warranty) for two years from the date of purchase. You can reklamieren — formally complain and demand remedy. The seller must repair the product (Nachbesserung) or replace it (Nachlieferung). If neither is possible, you may withdraw from the contract (Rücktritt) or reduce the price. This is a consumer right under German civil law (BGB § 437) and does not depend on any additional warranty (Garantie) offered by the manufacturer.

de.q: Warum muss man in Deutschland bei der Steuererklärung aufschreiben, ob man zu einer Kirche gehört oder nicht? Weil …
o: es eine Kirchensteuer gibt, die an die Einkommen- und Lohnsteuer geknüpft ist.
das für die Statistik in Deutschland wichtig ist.
man mehr Steuern zahlen muss, wenn man nicht zu einer Kirche gehört.
die Kirche für die Steuererklärung verantwortlich ist.

en.q: Why do you have to state in your tax return in Germany whether or not you belong to a church? Because …
o: there is a church tax (Kirchensteuer) that is linked to income tax and wage tax.
this is important for statistics in Germany.
you have to pay more taxes if you do not belong to a church.
the church is responsible for the tax return.

explanation.en: Germany collects a church tax (Kirchensteuer) that is calculated as a percentage of income/wage tax for registered church members, hence the need to declare church membership.

de.q: Die Menschen in Deutschland leben nach dem Grundsatz der religiösen Toleranz. Was bedeutet das?
o: Es dürfen keine Moscheen gebaut werden.
Jeder kann glauben, was er möchte.
Der Staat entscheidet, an welchen Gott die Menschen glauben.

en.q: People in Germany live according to the principle of religious tolerance. What does that mean?
o: Everyone can believe whatever they want.
The state decides which God people believe in.

explanation.en: Freedom of religion (Religionsfreiheit) means everyone can believe what they choose — including no religion at all — without state interference.

de.q: Was ist in Deutschland ein Brauch zu Ostern?

en.q: What is an Easter custom in Germany?
o: putting pumpkins in front of the door

explanation.en: Painting Easter eggs (Eier bemalen) is a traditional German Easter custom.

de.q: Pfingsten ist ein …

en.q: Pentecost (Pfingsten) is a …

explanation.en: Pfingsten (Pentecost) is a Christian holiday celebrated 50 days after Easter.

de.q: Welche Religion hat die europäische und deutsche Kultur geprägt?

en.q: Which religion has shaped European and German culture?

explanation.en: Christianity has historically shaped European and German culture, traditions, and institutions over many centuries.

de.q: In Deutschland nennt man die letzten vier Wochen vor Weihnachten …

en.q: In Germany, the last four weeks before Christmas are called …
o: the Day of Repentance and Prayer (Buß- und Bettag).

explanation.en: The four weeks before Christmas are called Advent (Adventszeit) in Germany.

de.q: Aus welchem Land sind die meisten Migrantinnen und Migranten nach Deutschland gekommen?

en.q: From which country have most migrants come to Germany?

explanation.en: Turkey is historically the largest source country of migrants to Germany, following the 1961 labor recruitment agreement.

de.q: In der DDR lebten vor allem Migrantinnen und Migranten aus …
